definition_zh: 独有的；专属的；排外的；高档的；独家新闻
definition_en: open only to a few people, belonging to one owner, or reported by a single newspaper
core_image: 门口的一道天鹅绒围绳
scene: 那家俱乐部只向会员开放，媒体一概不得入内。 The club is exclusive and admits members only.
sceneCN: 这里 exclusive 是「排外、高档的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：那家俱乐部只向会员开放，媒体一概不得入内。

senses.title: Only for some
senses.definition: limited to one person or group and not shared with others
senses.definitionCN: 只属于某个人或某个群体，不与外人共享
senses.example: The company holds exclusive rights to the design.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司拥有该设计的专有权。
senses.why: One owner keeps everything inside the rope.
senses.whyCN: 一个所有者把所有东西留在围绳之内。

senses.title: High status
senses.definition: used about places or groups that only wealthy or special people may enter
senses.definitionCN: 形容只允许富有或特殊人士进入的场所或群体
senses.example: They dined at an exclusive club by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河边一家高档俱乐部用餐。
senses.why: The closed door itself becomes a sign of status.
senses.whyCN: 紧闭的门本身就成了身份的象征。

senses.title: Single story
senses.definition: a news story printed or broadcast by only one newspaper or station
senses.definitionCN: 只由一家报纸或电台刊登、播出的新闻报道
senses.example: The paper ran an exclusive on the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 这家报纸刊登了关于合并的独家报道。
senses.why: One outlet owns the story, just as one owner holds the rights.
senses.whyCN: 一家媒体独占这条新闻，如同一个所有者独占权利。

intro.en: Exclusive comes from Latin excludere, to shut out.
intro.cn: exclusive 源自拉丁语 excludere，意为关在外面。

items.en: Claudere means to close.
items.cn: claudere 意为关闭。

items.en: Excludere joins ex-, out, with claudere, to close.
items.cn: excludere 由 ex-（出）与 claudere（关闭）组成。

items.en: Exclusivus describes something that shuts others out.
items.cn: exclusivus 形容把他人关在门外之物。

items.en: Medieval French exclusif keeps the sense of exclusion.
items.cn: 中古法语 exclusif 保留排除之意。

items.en: English exclusive adds the idea of high status.
items.cn: 英语 exclusive 增加了高档、专属的含义。

note.en: Exclusive shuts others out; inclusive lets them in.
note.cn: exclusive 把别人关在门外，inclusive 则把别人包含进来。

entries.definition: the act of leaving someone out
including everyone or everything
the state of belonging to one group only
carefully chosen and of high quality
for one person or group only
belonging to one owner only

normalIntro.en: Exclusive keeps the rope closed to outsiders.
normalIntro.cn: exclusive 让围绳对外人始终闭合。

normal.en: An exclusive club keeps outsiders at the door.
normal.cn: exclusive 俱乐部把外人挡在门口。

normal.en: Exclusive rights belong to one owner alone.
normal.cn: 专有权只属于一个所有者。

normal.en: Exclusive to means sold in one place only.
normal.cn: exclusive to 意为只在一个地方出售。

normal.en: An exclusive interview appears in one paper.
normal.cn: 独家采访只出现在一家报纸上。

normal.en: Exclusive of means not counting something.
normal.cn: exclusive of 意为不把某物计算在内。

abstract.en: Picture a velvet rope that only a few may cross.
abstract.cn: 想象一道只有少数人能越过的天鹅绒围绳。

abstract.en: Imagine one key that opens a single door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把只开一扇门的钥匙。

abstract.en: Think of a shop with just one customer inside.
abstract.cn: 想象店里只允许一位顾客进入。

examples.en: The brand signed an exclusive deal with the retailer.
examples.cn: 该品牌与零售商签了独家协议。

examples.en: Membership of the club is highly exclusive.
examples.cn: 该俱乐部的会员资格极为排外。

examples.en: The magazine published an exclusive about the star.
examples.cn: 杂志刊登了关于这位明星的独家报道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ clus（关）＋ ive」——把别人关在门外，只留自己人，就是独有的、排外的。

root: 拉丁语 excludere（关在外面）＝ ex-（出）＋ claudere（关闭）→ exclusive，核心义「只让少数人进入」。

sensesIntro.en: Exclusive means open only to a few, high in status, or reported by a single outlet.
sensesIntro.cn: exclusive 意为只对少数人开放、档次高，或由一家媒体独家报道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a velvet rope at the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口的一道天鹅绒围绳。

branches.en: Open only to one person or group.
branches.cn: 只对一个人或群体开放。

branches.en: The closed door signals high status.
branches.cn: 紧闭的门传递出高档身份。

branches.en: A single outlet owns the story.
branches.cn: 一家媒体独占这条新闻。

branches.en: Both senses rest on keeping others out.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在把他人挡在外面之上。

branches.en: What is exclusive is never shared widely.
branches.cn: 专属的东西从不广泛共享。

intro.en: Exclusive combines ex-, out, with Latin claudere, to close.
intro.cn: exclusive 由 ex-（出）与拉丁语 claudere（关闭）组成。

latinIntro.en: Excludere gives exclusivus and then English exclusive.
latinIntro.cn: excludere 给出 exclusivus，再到英语 exclusive。

items.example: Close and clause both trace to claudere.
items.exampleCN: close 与 clause 都可追溯到 claudere。
exclusivus 加上了形容词词尾。

latinEntries.example: Excludere is the source of exclusive.
latinEntries.exampleCN: excludere 是 exclusive 的来源。

definition_zh: 激怒；使烦躁；刺激（皮肤等）；使发炎
definition_en: to make someone angry or annoyed, or to make a part of the body sore and uncomfortable
core_image: 一根小刺反复蹭着同一块皮肤，人忍不住皱起眉
scene: 巴士晚了半小时，旁边的人一直用鞋跟敲地板。 The constant tapping began to irritate everyone in the queue.
sceneCN: 这里 irritate 是「使烦躁」（第 1 个义项：反复刺激引起不耐烦），句意为那不停的敲击开始让排队的每个人都烦躁起来。画面里的物件：鞋跟、地板、排队的栏杆。

pos.zh: 动词：激怒；使烦躁；刺激；使发炎

derivatives.zh: 由 irritate 加 -ion 构成，义为「恼怒；刺激；发炎」
由 irritate 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人恼火的」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「恼火的；发炎的」
由拉丁 irritabilis 而来，加 -able 后缀，义为「易怒的」

senses.title: To make someone annoyed
senses.definition: to make someone feel annoyed, often by something small and repeated
senses.definitionCN: 用细小而反复的举动让人不耐烦、恼火
senses.example: Loud chewing at the next desk irritates her every day.
senses.exampleCN: 邻桌大声咀嚼每天都让她烦躁。
senses.why: The Latin verb irritare meant to provoke, and provocation starts with a small repeated prod.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 irritare 本义是「挑动、激怒」，挑动的起点正是一下又一下的小刺。

senses.title: To make a body part sore
senses.definition: to cause a part of the body, especially skin or eyes, to become sore, red, or itchy
senses.definitionCN: 使皮肤、眼睛等部位发红、发痒或不适
senses.example: This wool sweater irritates my neck.
senses.exampleCN: 这件羊毛衫刺得我脖子发痒。
senses.why: The bodily sense grows straight out of the physical prick that the word first named.
senses.whyCN: 身体义直接从这个词最初指的「扎、刺」长出来，皮肤被扎就会发红发痒。

senses.title: To cause inflammation
senses.definition: to make tissue become inflamed or painful, as an injury or substance can
senses.definitionCN: 使组织发炎、疼痛，如外伤或刺激物所致
senses.example: The smoke irritated his lungs during the fire drill.
senses.exampleCN: 消防演习时烟雾刺激得他肺部发炎。
senses.why: Inflammation is the body-level result of repeated irritation, so the verb extends to medicine.
senses.whyCN: 发炎是反复受刺激在身体层面的结果，于是这个词延伸进医学语境。

senses.title: To provoke a reaction
senses.definition: to stir up a feeling or response in someone, often deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 有意激起某人的某种情绪或反应
senses.example: The question irritated a heated argument in the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 那个问题在会议里激起了一场激烈争论。
senses.why: Provoking an emotion is the same push as provoking a person, only the target is a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 激起情绪和激怒一个人是同一种「推」，只是对象换成了感受。

senses.title: To bother mechanically
senses.definition: to disturb a device or process slightly so that it stops working smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 轻微干扰装置或过程，使其不能顺畅运行
senses.example: Dust irritated the old printer until it jammed again.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘搅得那台旧打印机又卡纸了。
senses.why: The extended sense keeps the image of a small foreign thing repeatedly rubbing a mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 这个引申义保留了「小异物反复摩擦机械」的画面。

intro.en: Irritate goes back to Latin irritare, "to provoke, excite, exasperate", a verb of uncertain deeper origin.
intro.cn: irritate 可追到拉丁语 irritare「挑动、激怒」，更深层的来源一般认为不确定。

items.en: irritare meant to provoke or stir up, and irritatus was its past participle.
items.cn: irritare 意为挑动、激起，过去分词是 irritatus。

items.en: The verb also named making something rough or sore, a bodily prick.
items.cn: 这个词还指把东西弄粗糙、弄痛，是一次身体上的刺。

items.en: Church and medical Latin kept irritatio for provocation and bodily soreness.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语的 irritatio 兼指激怒与身体刺痛。

items.en: English took irritate in the sixteenth century for provoking anger.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 irritate，表示激怒。

items.en: The medical sense of inflamed tissue developed alongside the everyday one.
items.cn: 组织发炎的医学义与日常义一起发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin irrit- stem; the near-meaning group holds words for annoying and for stirring feelings.
note.cn: 形近组共用拉丁词干 irrit-；近义组收表示惹恼和激起情绪的词。

entries.definition: The feeling of being annoyed, or a sore spot on the skin.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「恼怒；刺痛处」，同族名词。

entries.definition: Annoyed, or red and sore.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词转形容词，义为「恼火的；发红的」。

entries.definition: Easily annoyed.
entries.definitionCN: 同源形容词，义为「易怒的」，后缀为 -able。

entries.definition: To make someone slightly angry.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「惹恼」，程度比 irritate 轻，来源不同。

entries.definition: To stir someone into a reaction on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「挑动、激起」，强调有意为之。

entries.definition: To disturb or trouble someone.

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the Latin provocation to the everyday wool-collar feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「挑动」走到毛衣领子扎脖子的日常感受。

normal.en: Latin irritare meant to provoke or stir up.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 irritare 意为挑动、激起。

normal.en: The same root gives irritation and irritable.
normal.cn: 同一词根生出 irritation 与 irritable。

normal.en: Be irritated by is the usual passive pattern.
normal.cn: be irritated by 是常见的被动搭配。

normal.en: Skin and eyes are what wool and smoke irritate.
normal.cn: 羊毛与烟刺激的是皮肤和眼睛。

normal.en: An irritating habit is a small thing done again and again.
normal.cn: irritating habit 就是反复做的小动作。

abstract.en: Irritation is a splinter that keeps touching the same spot.
abstract.cn: 烦躁是一根总碰在同一处的木刺。

abstract.en: To irritate is to push a feeling until it answers.
abstract.cn: 激怒就是把一种情绪推到它应答为止。

abstract.en: Every repeated small sound becomes an irritant.
abstract.cn: 每一个反复的小声音都会变成刺激源。

examples.en: He was irritated by the noise from the street.
examples.cn: 他被街上的噪音弄得烦躁。

examples.en: Strong perfume can irritate the eyes and throat.
examples.cn: 浓香水会刺激眼睛和喉咙。

examples.en: The teacher's slow questions irritated the whole class.
examples.cn: 老师慢吞吞的提问让全班都烦了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一日的头痛」—— 每天一点点，把人磨得烦躁

root: 拉丁语 irritare「挑动、激怒」→ irritatus → 英语 irritate。同族有 irritation、irritating、irritable。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: annoying a person, sore skin, inflamed tissue, stirred-up feelings, and a slightly disturbed mechanism.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：惹人烦躁、刺激皮肤、使发炎、激起情绪反应，以及轻微搅扰机械。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small sharp point rubbing the same place again and again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小尖点反复蹭同一处。

branches.en: THE DESK: a small sound that wears patience down.
branches.cn: 书桌这条线：小声音把耐心磨光。

branches.en: THE COLLAR: wool against skin until it itches.
branches.cn: 领口这条线：羊毛贴着皮肤直到发痒。

branches.en: THE LUNG: smoke turning irritation into inflammation.
branches.cn: 肺这条线：烟把刺激变成发炎。

branches.en: THE MEETING: one question stirring a whole argument.
branches.cn: 会议这条线：一个问题激起全场争论。

branches.en: THE PRINTER: dust making a machine stutter.
branches.cn: 打印机这条线：灰尘让机器打嗝。

intro.en: Irritate is a borrowed Latin verb; English adds only verb endings and noun or adjective suffixes.
intro.cn: irritate 是整体借来的拉丁动词，英语只添了动词词尾与名词、形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives share the irrit- stem, from irritare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词共用 irrit- 词干，源自 irritare。

items.example: The stem of the whole family.
A Romance cousin of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 同一动词的罗曼语亲属。

items.meaningCN: 构成表示主动的形容词
构成表示感受的形容词

definition_zh: 尼龙；尼龙织物；尼龙长袜；尼龙制的；尼龙商标名
definition_en: a strong artificial fibre made from polyamide, the cloth or stockings woven from it, and the registered trade name that first named the material
core_image: 一缕极细的透明丝线从机器的细孔里被拉出，绕成一卷柔韧的纤维
scene: 战后百货商店的柜台前，售货员把一双薄得透光的长袜摊开给顾客看。 The assistant stretched a pair of nylon stockings to show how thin they were.
sceneCN: 这里的 nylon 指「尼龙长袜」（第 2 个义项：用尼龙织成的衣物）；句意为售货员把一双尼龙长袜拉开，让顾客看它有多薄。图中可辨识物件：玻璃柜台、长袜、价签。

pos.zh: 尼龙；尼龙织物；尼龙长袜

derivatives.zh: 由 nylon 加复数 -s 构成，固定指「尼龙长袜」
由 nylon 与 coated 复合而成，义为「尼龙涂层的」

senses.title: A strong synthetic fibre
senses.definition: a strong, light synthetic fibre made from polyamide, used for thread, rope, fabric and many solid parts
senses.definitionCN: 由聚酰胺制成的结实而轻的合成纤维，用于线、绳、织物以及许多固体部件
senses.example: The tent is made of light nylon that dries quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 这顶帐篷用干得快的轻质尼龙制成。
senses.why: The word began as a trade name for one new polyamide fibre, and the material itself is still the sense people meet first.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初只是一种新型聚酰胺纤维的商品名，而这种材料本身仍是人们最先接触到的义项。

senses.title: Cloth or stockings made from this fibre
senses.definition: cloth woven from nylon, especially the thin stockings that made the fibre famous
senses.definitionCN: 用尼龙织成的布，尤指让这种纤维一举成名的薄长袜
senses.example: She wore black nylons to the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她去面试时穿了黑色尼龙长袜。
senses.why: Once a fibre is woven, the product can take the fibre's name, and the plural nylons became a fixed word for stockings.
senses.whyCN: 纤维一旦织成布，成品就能沿用纤维的名字，复数 nylons 也固定成了「长袜」的说法。

senses.title: Made of nylon, used before a noun
senses.definition: made from nylon, used directly before a noun to describe an object
senses.definitionCN: 用尼龙制成的，直接放在名词前描述物体
senses.example: He packed a nylon jacket for the rainy week.
senses.exampleCN: 他为多雨的一周装了一件尼龙夹克。
senses.why: Because the material is named by a noun, English simply puts that noun in front of another noun instead of making a separate adjective.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种材料本身用名词命名，英语直接把名词放在另一个名词前，而不另造形容词。

senses.title: The registered trade name behind the material
senses.definition: the registered trade name introduced in the nineteen thirties for the first of these polyamide fibres
senses.definitionCN: 二十世纪三十年代为最早这种聚酰胺纤维推出的注册商标名
senses.example: The company chose the trade name before the fibre reached the shops.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在纤维上市之前就选定了这个商品名。
senses.why: A coined brand name can become the ordinary word for a whole class of products, and nylon made that journey within a single generation.
senses.whyCN: 一个生造的品牌名可以变成整类产品的普通名称，而 nylon 在一代人之内就走完了这段路。

intro.en: Nylon is a coined trade name of the nineteen thirties rather than an inherited word; its exact inspiration is uncertain, and no Latin root lies behind it.
intro.cn: nylon 是二十世纪三十年代生造的商品名，不是继承下来的词；它确切的灵感来源不确定，背后也没有拉丁词根。

items.en: Chemists developed a strong polyamide fibre as a substitute for silk, and the material needed a commercial name before it could be sold.
items.cn: 化学家研制出一种结实的聚酰胺纤维来替代蚕丝，这种材料在上市前需要一个商业名称。

items.en: The company registered nylon as a trade name, and the coined word was chosen chiefly because it was short, easy to say and unlikely to clash with existing marks.
items.cn: 公司把 nylon 注册为商品名，这个生造词被选中，主要是因为简短、好念，且不易与已有的商标冲突。

items.en: A common story says the word blends the initials of two cities, but the company has denied any such formula, so the origin is best treated as uncertain.
items.cn: 流传的一种说法称这个词由两座城市的首字母拼成，但公司否认存在这类公式，因此其来源最好视为不确定。

items.en: Within a few years the brand name was used for the fibre itself and for stockings, and dictionaries recorded it as an ordinary noun.
items.cn: 不出几年，这个品牌名就被用来指纤维本身和长袜，词典也把它收作普通名词。

items.en: Modern English uses nylon for the material, for nylon cloth and, in the plural, for stockings, while the brand right still belongs to its owner.
items.cn: 现代英语用 nylon 指材料、尼龙布，复数形式指长袜，而商标权仍归其所有者。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words whose spelling or ending echoes nylon; the near-meaning group collects other fibres and textile terms.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或词尾与 nylon 相呼应的词；近义组收其他纤维与织物用语。

entries.definition: A colourless gas used in bright advertising lights; the spelling is close but the source is Greek.
entries.definitionCN: 一种用于明亮广告灯的无色气体；拼写相近，但来源是希腊语，词源不同。

entries.definition: A negatively charged ion; the -on ending looks familiar but the source is Greek.
entries.definitionCN: 带负电的离子；词尾 -on 看着眼熟，但来源是希腊语，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: The plural of the fibre name, used as a noun for stockings.
entries.definitionCN: 纤维名的复数形式，固定作名词指尼龙长袜。

entries.definition: A synthetic fibre made from esters, widely used in clothing.
entries.definitionCN: 由酯类制成的合成纤维，广泛用于制衣。

entries.definition: A semi-synthetic fibre made from cellulose.
entries.definitionCN: 由纤维素制成的半合成纤维；人造丝。

entries.definition: A synthetic fibre often used in warm knitwear.
entries.definitionCN: 常用于保暖针织品的合成纤维；腈纶。

entries.definition: A thin thread of natural or artificial material.
entries.definitionCN: 天然或人造材料制成的细丝；纤维。

normalIntro.en: Nylon is a brand name that turned into a material word, so its memory hooks are the year, the company, the sound of the ending and the stockings it made famous.
normalIntro.cn: nylon 是由品牌名变成的材料词，所以记忆钩子包括年代、公司、词尾的读音，以及它捧红的长袜。

normal.en: The word was coined and registered in 1938, so it has a birthday rather than a Latin ancestry.
normal.cn: 这个词于一九三八年被生造并注册，所以它有生日，而不是拉丁血统。

normal.en: Its ending -on makes it sound like a chemical fibre, the same sound heard in rayon and orlon.
normal.cn: 词尾 -on 让它听起来像化学纤维，rayon 与 orlon 也带着同样的声音。

normal.en: The plural nylons is not just more than one nylon but a fixed word for stockings.
normal.cn: 复数 nylons 不只是「不止一个 nylon」，而是固定指长袜的词。

normal.en: Compounds like nylon rope and nylon thread simply put the material in front of the object.
normal.cn: nylon rope 与 nylon thread 这类复合词，只是把材料放在物体前面。

normal.en: The brand name became generic, the way many successful trade names turn into everyday nouns.
normal.cn: 这个品牌名变成了通名，就像许多成功的商标名变成日常名词一样。

abstract.en: A word with no root is still a word: nylon shows that a name can be invented and then made real by use.
abstract.cn: 没有词根的词依然是词：nylon 说明一个名字可以被发明，再被使用变成真的。

abstract.en: The fibre replaced silk by imitating what silk did, which is how many new materials enter ordinary life.
abstract.cn: 这种纤维靠模仿蚕丝的功用取代了蚕丝，许多新材料正是这样进入日常生活的。

abstract.en: That a brand name became the name of the material suggests how quickly English absorbs whatever it needs to name.
abstract.cn: 品牌名变成了材料名，说明英语吸收它需要命名的东西有多快。

examples.en: The parachute is packed in a bag of strong nylon.
examples.cn: 降落伞收在一只结实的尼龙袋里。

examples.en: Nylon dries fast, so it is popular for rain jackets.
examples.cn: 尼龙干得快，因此很受雨衣欢迎。

examples.en: She bought three pairs of nylons at the department store.
examples.cn: 她在百货商店买了三双尼龙长袜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「耐纶」——又结实又耐磨的纶线；记住 nylon 是尼龙。

root: 二十世纪三十年代杜邦公司注册的商品名，词源为生造，确切灵感不确定；由专有商标转为普通名词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one invented fibre; from it come the cloth, the stockings, the attributive use and the trade name that still sits behind the word.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种被发明出来的纤维；由此分出尼龙布、长袜、定语用法，以及仍然待在这个词背后的商标名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thread of clear fibre pulled from a fine nozzle and wound into a soft coil.
core.cn: 核心意象：一缕透明纤维从细孔中被拉出，绕成一卷柔韧的线。

branches.en: a coil of fine thread on a factory spool
branches.cn: 工厂线轴上的一卷细丝

branches.en: a drawer full of thin stockings
branches.cn: 抽屉里满是薄长袜

branches.en: a light jacket hanging by the door
branches.cn: 门边挂着的一件轻便夹克

branches.en: a trademark filed in an office
branches.cn: 在事务所里备案的商标

branches.en: one fibre moving from factory to wardrobe
branches.cn: 一种纤维从工厂走进衣柜

intro.en: Nylon is a coined name, so its parts are not true affixes; the entries below trace the chemical and textile words that grew around it, plus the plural ending it takes.
intro.cn: nylon 是生造名，组成部分并非真正的词缀；下面列的是围绕它生长起来的化学与纺织用语，以及它采用的复数词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded, because the word was invented as a trade name in the twentieth century.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词在二十世纪作为商品名被造出来，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

a thin thread used in textiles
made by chemical rather than natural means
cloth made by weaving or knitting
a close-fitting covering for the leg and foot

definition_zh: 许可；许可证；执照；正式批准；授权使用
definition_en: official permission to do something, the document that proves it, or the act of granting such permission
core_image: 权威递出的一把钥匙：门原本锁着，得到许可的人才能推开
scene: 市政厅窗口前，申请人接过盖了钢印的执照。 The clerk handed over the business license, and the applicant put it in the same folder as her driving permit.
sceneCN: 这里 license 是「官方许可证」，也落在纸质证件这一层（第 1、2 个义项：官方许可；证明许可的证件）；句意：工作人员递过营业执照，申请人把它和驾驶证一起放进文件夹。图中可辨识物件：市政厅窗口、盖钢印的执照、文件夹、驾照；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 许可证；执照；许可；自由、放纵（古义/文学）
正式批准；给……发许可证；授权使用

collocations.zh: 经许可（授权生产或使用）
诗的破格；艺术上的自由处理

derivatives.zh: 许可的颁发；执业许可制度

senses.title: Permission granted by an authority
senses.titleCN: 官方许可：权威解除禁令
senses.definition: official permission from a government or other authority to do something that is otherwise controlled or forbidden
senses.definitionCN: 政府或其他权威机构给予的正式许可，使原本受管制或被禁止的事可以做
senses.example: The company applied for a license to drill in the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司申请在海湾钻探的许可证。
senses.why: The Latin source is licere 'to be allowed', and its noun licentia meant 'freedom, permission'. The core scene is not a piece of paper but a gatekeeper lifting a ban, so the first sense is the permission itself; it can even be uncountable, as in work under license.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头是 licere“被允许”，其名词 licentia 意为“自由、许可”。核心画面不是一张纸，而是守门人解除禁令，所以第一义项是许可本身；它甚至可作不可数用法，如 work under license（经许可工作）。

senses.title: The document that carries the permission
senses.titleCN: 执照：把许可变成可携带的证件
senses.definition: an official card, certificate, or document that shows the holder has been given permission to do something
senses.definitionCN: 表明持有人已获准做某事的官方卡片、证书或文件
senses.example: He handed his driver's license to the officer at the checkpoint.
senses.exampleCN: 他在检查站把驾照递给了警官。
senses.why: Permission needs proof once it leaves the office. By metonymy the abstract grant becomes the object in your pocket: a driver's license, a business license, a hunting license. This is the countable, everyday sense and the one that takes a plural.
senses.whyCN: 许可一旦离开办公室就需要凭证。借代让抽象的授予变成口袋里的实物：驾照、营业执照、狩猎证。这是可数、最日常的义项，也是能变复数的那个。

senses.title: A contract granting rights to use a work
senses.titleCN: 授权协议：允许他人使用作品或权利
senses.definition: a legal agreement under which the owner of a copyright, patent, or trademark allows another party to use it, usually for a fee
senses.definitionCN: 版权、专利或商标所有人允许另一方使用其权利的法律协议，通常收取费用
senses.example: The publisher bought a license to translate the novel into Chinese.
senses.exampleCN: 出版社买下了把这部小说译成中文的授权。
senses.why: Here licentia is narrowed from general permission to one specified right. The owner keeps ownership and hands over only a limited freedom, which is why a license is signed rather than sold: the thing granted is use, not title.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 licentia 从笼统许可收窄为一项特定权利。所有人保留所有权，只交出一部分有限自由，所以 license 是“签授权”而不是“卖断”：授予的是使用权，不是所有权。

senses.title: Literary liberty: freedom without restraint
senses.titleCN: 放纵的自由：不受约束的状态（古义/文学）
senses.definition: freedom to act as one pleases, especially when it goes beyond accepted limits; an older literary sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 想怎么做就怎么做的自由，尤指超出公认界限；该词较古老的文学义
senses.example: During the carnival, a spirit of license swept through the streets.
senses.exampleCN: 狂欢节期间，一种放纵的自由气息席卷街头。
senses.why: Latin licentia could mean both 'permission' and 'unrestrained freedom'. English kept the second branch: a license can be a state of liberty, not a document. Modern British usage usually spells this noun licence, while the verb remains license.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 licentia 既可指“许可”，也可指“不受约束的自由”。英语保留了第二条分支：license 可以是自由状态而非文件。现代英式英语中该名词通常拼作 licence，动词仍作 license。

senses.title: To authorize an activity officially
senses.titleCN: 正式批准：官方放行某项活动
senses.definition: to give official permission for an activity, or to issue a permit to a person or business
senses.definitionCN: 正式批准某项活动，或向个人、企业发放许可证
senses.example: Only the city can license a new restaurant kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 只有市政府才能给新的餐馆厨房发许可证。
senses.why: The verb is recorded from about 1400 and was formed directly from the noun. The authority is the subject, the permitted activity is the object, and the act is a formal yes rather than a description of freedom.
senses.whyCN: 动词约在 1400 年出现，直接由名词转化而来。主语是权威机构，宾语是被批准的活动，这个动作是一个正式的“可以”，而不是对自由状态的描述。

senses.title: To grant the right to use intellectual property
senses.titleCN: 授权使用：把知识产权许可出去
senses.definition: to give a person or company legal permission to use a copyrighted work, invention, or brand
senses.definitionCN: 给予个人或公司使用受版权保护的作品、发明或品牌的法律许可
senses.example: The studio licensed the character for a series of toys.
senses.exampleCN: 工作室把这个角色的使用权授权给了一系列玩具。
senses.why: This is sense 3 as a verb. The owner stays the owner and lets someone else exploit the right; the object is a work or a right, not an activity, which separates it from license a restaurant in sense 5.
senses.whyCN: 这是第 3 义项的动词化。所有人仍是所有人，只允许别人利用这项权利；宾语是作品或权利，而不是活动，因此区别于第 5 义项的“给餐馆发证”。

senses.title: Social permission: a reason to speak or act
senses.titleCN: 理据性许可：有理由开口或行动
senses.definition: a fact, status, or circumstance that gives someone the freedom or justification to do something
senses.definitionCN: 某种事实、身份或情境给予某人做某事的自由或正当理由
senses.example: Twenty years of service gave her license to question the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 二十年的服务经历给了她质疑这项计划的底气。
senses.why: No office is involved. The authority is experience, rank, or custom, and the phrase a license to do something treats that social standing as a grant. The word still performs the same act: it removes the risk of being thought out of line.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有发证机关。权威是经验、地位或惯例，而 a license to do something 这一说法把社会身份当成一种授予。这个词仍在做同一件事：消除“越界”的顾虑。

senses.title: Artistic license: the right to break the rules
senses.titleCN: 艺术破格：为效果而偏离事实或规则
senses.definition: the freedom that artists, writers, or performers claim to change facts, rules, or language in order to achieve an effect
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家、作家或表演者为达到效果而改变事实、规则或语言时自称的自由
senses.example: The film takes poetic license with the historical record.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影对历史记载做了诗意的破格处理。
senses.why: The fixed phrase poetic license shows the word at its most permissive: the permission comes from convention rather than an office, and the deviation is expected to serve the work rather than deceive the audience.
senses.whyCN: 固定短语 poetic license 展示了这个词最宽松的一面：许可来自惯例而不是机关，而这种偏离被期待是服务于作品，而不是欺骗观众。

senses.title: Fixed compounds and the licence/license spelling line
senses.titleCN: 固定搭配与拼写边界：license plate、licence/license
senses.definition: the noun as it survives in fixed compounds such as license plate, and the British and American rules that separate the noun licence from the verb license
senses.definitionCN: 名词在 license plate 等固定搭配中的用法，以及英式、美式把名词 licence 与动词 license 分开的拼写规则
senses.example: In British English the noun is licence and the verb is license; American English uses license for both.
senses.exampleCN: 英式英语中名词是 licence、动词是 license；美式英语两者都用 license。
senses.why: Compounds freeze the noun, which is why American license plate keeps the s. The spelling split follows the French-derived noun and the later English verb, standardized differently in Britain and America in the 18th and 19th centuries; in Britain the c marks the noun, the s marks the verb.
senses.whyCN: 复合词把名词形式固定下来，所以美式 license plate 保留 s。拼写分裂则源于法语来源的名词与后来英语派生的动词，18—19 世纪在英美分别被标准化成不同规则；英式用 c 标记名词、用 s 标记动词。

intro.en: License is a permission word, not a law word. Latin licere 'to be allowed, to be lawful' produced licentia 'freedom, permission', which Old French passed to English as licence. The modern split between the noun and the verb, and between British and American spelling, came much later.
intro.cn: license 是“许可”词，不是“法律”词。拉丁语 licere“被允许、合法”产生名词 licentia“自由、许可”，古法语把 licence 传给英语。名词与动词的分工、以及英美拼写的差异，都是后来才形成的。

items.en: Latin licere 'to be allowed, to be lawful' gave the noun licentia 'freedom, permission, license' and the participle licitus 'allowed'. The core idea is permission granted, not a statute enacted.
items.cn: 拉丁语 licere“被允许、合法”产生了名词 licentia“自由、许可、执照”和分词 licitus“获准的”。核心观念是“被授予许可”，而不是“制定法律”。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain. Licere is generally thought to go back to a PIE root *leik- 'to offer, bargain', also seen in Latin liceri 'to bid at auction'; this is a reconstruction, not a documented fact, and the intermediate steps are not certain.
items.cn: 更深的来源不确定。一般认为 licere 可追溯到原始印欧语词根 *leik-“出价、议价”，也见于拉丁语 liceri“拍卖出价”；这属于构拟，不是有文献确证的事实，中间环节并不确定。

items.en: Old French licence (12c.–13c.) meant 'freedom, liberty, permission' and came from Latin licentia. English borrowed the word rather than building it from parts.
items.cn: 古法语 licence（12—13 世纪）意为“自由、自主、许可”，来自拉丁语 licentia。英语是整词借入，而不是自己用词素拼出来的。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English in the late 14c. with both 'liberty, freedom' and 'formal permission from a superior'. The verb appears about 1400 as 'to give formal authority', and a 'give free rein' sense is recorded in the 1530s.
items.cn: 名词在 14 世纪晚期的英语中已有记录，兼有“自由、自主”和“上级的正式许可”两义。动词约 1400 年出现，意为“授予正式权限”；“放任、放开”义见于 16 世纪 30 年代。

items.en: The freedom branch stayed strong in the 16c.–17c., when licentious 'morally unrestrained' entered English from licentiosus. The permit branch gradually became the dominant everyday meaning, leaving the freedom branch as literary and archaic.
items.cn: “自由、放纵”这一支在 16—17 世纪仍很活跃，licentious“道德上无节制”就是此时从 licentiosus 进入英语的。此后“许可证”这一支逐渐成为日常主义，“自由”义退居文学与古旧用法。

items.en: License is not from Latin lex 'law' (genitive legis), which belongs to a different root and gives legal and legislate; the two words talk about rules but are not related. British English keeps licence for the noun and license for the verb; American English uses license for both. Compounds such as license plate, license fee and license holder keep the noun form.
items.cn: license 并非出自拉丁语 lex“法律”（属格 legis）；lex 属于另一个词根，衍生出 legal、legislate。两个词都谈规则，却不同源。英式英语名词用 licence、动词用 license；美式英语两者都用 license。license plate、license fee、license holder 等复合词则固定保留名词形式。

note.en: The look-alikes either belong to the Latin licere family or mark the noun/verb spelling line; the near synonyms each grant permission from a different angle.
note.cn: 第一组要么属于拉丁语 licere 词族，要么标记名词与动词的拼写分界；第二组则从不同角度表达“准许”。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the noun only. British usage keeps licence for the permission or the document and license for the verb; American usage uses license for both.
entries.definitionCN: 只用于英式名词的拼写。英式用法中，表示许可或许可证的名词作 licence，动词作 license；美式则两者都用 license。

entries.definition: Lawful or permitted, from Latin licitus, the participle of licere. It is an adjective, not a permit, and has no verb use.
entries.definitionCN: 合法的、获准的，来自拉丁语 licitus（licere 的分词）。它是形容词，不指证件，也没有动词用法。

entries.definition: Morally unrestrained, especially in sexual matters, from licentia 'freedom' plus -osus 'full of'. It carries only the excessive-liberty branch, never the permit branch.
entries.definitionCN: 道德上无节制的，尤指性方面，来自 licentia“自由”加 -osus“充满……的”。它只继承“过度自由”这一支，从不表示许可证。

entries.definition: To allow something, or an official document that allows it. It is the closest everyday synonym, though a permit is often a specific written allowance such as a parking permit, while a license usually certifies a professional or legal right.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某事，或允许做某事的官方文件。它是最接近的日常同义词；但 permit 多指具体的书面允许（如停车证），而 license 常指对专业资格或法律权利的认证。

entries.definition: The act of allowing or the state of being allowed. It names the abstract grant only, never the card in your pocket, and it has no verb sense of issuing a license.
entries.definitionCN: 允许的行为或被允许的状态。它只指抽象的授予，不指口袋里的证件，也没有“发许可证”的动词义。

entries.definition: Official power or approval to act. It stresses the authority behind the grant rather than the paper or the freedom that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的官方权力或批准。它强调授予背后的权威，而不是证件本身或随之而来的自由。

entries.definition: A right granted by a company or government to sell goods or run a service under its name. It is a kind of license, but tied to a brand or a monopoly rather than to a single activity.
entries.definitionCN: 公司或政府授予的、以其名义销售商品或经营服务的权利。它是许可的一种，但绑定品牌或垄断经营权，而不是单项活动。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin licere 'to be allowed' plus -entia, with licit, illicit, licentious and leisure in the same Latin family.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：拉丁语 licere“被允许”加 -entia，licit、illicit、licentious、leisure 都在同一个拉丁词族里。

normal.en: licere means 'to be allowed'. License is the allowed-ness itself, before it is ever a card in a wallet.
normal.cn: licere 意为“被允许”。license 首先就是这种“获准状态”，然后才变成钱包里的卡片。

normal.en: licentia covered both 'permission' and 'freedom'. The modern word still keeps the old freedom branch in literary use, as in a spirit of license.
normal.cn: licentia 兼有“许可”与“自由”两义。现代英语仍在文学语境里保留“自由”这一支，如 a spirit of license（放纵的气息）。

normal.en: The paper sense is a metonymy: the grant stands for the document that proves it, so a driver's license is both permission and proof.
normal.cn: 证件义是借代：授予本身代替了证明它的文件，所以 driver's license 既是许可也是凭证。

normal.en: Do not connect license to lex 'law'. Lex is about statutes and gives legal and legislate; licere is about being permitted, and the two only happen to talk about rules.
normal.cn: 不要把 license 连到 lex“法律”。lex 指成文法规，衍生出 legal、legislate；licere 指“被允许”，两者只是碰巧都谈规则。

normal.en: Spelling: British noun licence, British verb license; American both license. The c/s line marks word class, not a difference in meaning.
normal.cn: 拼写：英式名词 licence、动词 license；美式两者都写 license。c 与 s 这条线标记的是词性，不是意义差别。

abstract.en: Picture a locked door with a guard. License is the guard stepping aside — the permission itself, not the door and not the key.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇锁着的门和一名守卫。license 是守卫让开的那一下——是许可本身，不是门，也不是钥匙。

abstract.en: Then the guard hands you a card so that other guards will step aside too. That card is the second sense, the license you carry.
abstract.cn: 然后守卫递给你一张卡，好让别的守卫也让开。那张卡就是第 2 义项，你随身携带的许可证。

abstract.en: When there is no guard at all, license becomes the freedom to act, which is why poets claim poetic license to break the rules on purpose.
abstract.cn: 当根本没有守卫时，license 就变成行动的自由；诗人正是据此主张 poetic license，故意打破规则。

examples.en: The university licenses its software to students at a reduced fee.
examples.cn: 这所大学以优惠价格把软件授权给学生使用。

examples.en: Her position gave her license to challenge the chair.
examples.cn: 她的职位给了她质疑主席的底气。

examples.en: In British English, licence is the noun and license is the verb.
examples.cn: 在英式英语中，licence 是名词，license 是动词。

dict_mnemonic.text: “来sense”——官方来了这份许可，事情才 sense 得通 → license 许可证；许可

root: 拉丁语 licere“被允许、合法”→ 名词 licentia“许可、自由”。核心是“权威解除禁令、放行”，再由“许可”引申出证件、授权协议、自由放纵与艺术破格；与 lex“法律”并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of license, one movement: an authority lifts a ban, the permission becomes a document, then a limited right, then a social justification, and finally a freedom that needs no office at all.
sensesIntro.cn: license 的九个义项是一条线：权威解除禁令，许可变成证件，再收窄为有限权利，又转成社会层面的底气，最后成为无需发证机关的自由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an authority hands over a key, and a door that was locked can now be opened.
core.cn: 核心意象：权威递出一把钥匙，原本锁着的门现在可以被推开。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: an authority lifts a ban, and the verb is that lifting done officially and out loud.
branches.cn: 权威：权威解除禁令，动词就是这一解除被正式、公开地做出。

branches.en: PAPER: permission becomes a document you carry, and compounds plus spelling freeze its noun form.
branches.cn: 纸面：许可变成随身携带的证件，而复合词与拼写规则又把名词形式固定下来。

branches.en: RIGHTS: a limited right is granted while ownership stays with the owner, in both the noun and the verb.
branches.cn: 权利：只授予有限使用权，所有权仍留给所有人；名词与动词都走这一支。

branches.en: FREEDOM: from unrestrained liberty to the artist's licensed deviation from fact and rule.
branches.cn: 自由：从不受约束的放纵，到艺术家获准偏离事实与规则。

branches.en: JUSTIFICATION: status, experience or custom acts as the authority that grants the permission.
branches.cn: 理据：地位、经验或惯例充当授予许可的“权威”。

intro.en: License is a borrowed Latin noun, not an English prefix-plus-root construction. English adds only ordinary suffixes such as -ed, -ee, -or and -ure; the endings -nce and -nse belong to the borrowed word itself.
intro.cn: license 是借入的拉丁名词，不是英语“前缀＋词根”的构造。英语只加 -ed、-ee、-or、-ure 这类普通后缀；-nce 与 -nse 的词尾属于借词本身。

latinIntro.en: Inside Latin, licere produced licentia and licitus, and those yielded English licence/license, licit, illicit and licentious. Leisure reaches English through Old French and is generally traced to the same licere.
latinIntro.cn: 在拉丁语内部，licere 产生了 licentia 与 licitus，后者衍生出英语的 licence/license、licit、illicit、licentious。leisure 经古法语进入英语，一般也追溯到同一个 licere。

items.structure: license + -ed (past participle used as an adjective)
items.meaning: having official permission to do something
items.meaningCN: 已获官方许可的；持证的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: Only licensed drivers may use this road.
items.exampleCN: 只有持证司机才能使用这条路。

items.meaning: a person or company that has been given a license
items.meaningCN: 被许可人；持证人（-ee 表示接受者）
items.example: The licensee must renew the permit every year.
items.exampleCN: 被许可人必须每年续办许可证。

items.meaning: the party that grants a license to another party
items.meaningCN: 许可人；授权方（-or 表示施动者）
items.example: The licensor keeps ownership of the trademark.
items.exampleCN: 许可人保留该商标的所有权。

items.meaning: the act or system of granting licenses, especially for a profession
items.meaningCN: 许可的颁发；执业许可制度（-ure 构成行为或状态名词）
items.example: Nursing licensure requires a state examination.
items.exampleCN: 护士执业许可需要参加州级考试。

items.meaning: to be allowed, to be permitted
items.example: The verb is the permission behind every sense of license.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 license 各义项背后的“许可”。

items.example: Latin licentia already carried both permission and excess.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 licentia 已同时带有“许可”与“放纵”。

items.example: Its opposite illicit marks what the law forbids.
items.exampleCN: 它的反义词 illicit 标出法律禁止之事。

items.example: It forms licensure, the granting of licences.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 licensure，即执照的颁发。

items.example: The city fined the unlicensed vendor.
items.exampleCN: 市政对那个无照摊贩开了罚单。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 合法的；获准的（与 license 同源，保留拉丁分词义）

latinEntries.meaning: not allowed by law or custom
latinEntries.meaningCN: 非法的；违禁的；不正当的

latinEntries.meaning: morally unrestrained, especially in sexual matters
latinEntries.meaningCN: 放荡的；无节制的（只继承“过度自由”义）

latinEntries.structure: Old French leisir, generally traced to Latin licere (to be allowed)
latinEntries.meaning: free time, time at one's disposal
latinEntries.meaningCN: 闲暇；空闲时间（本义一般认为是“被允许自由支配的时间”）

definition_zh: 更可取的；较好的；更合意的；更适宜的
definition_en: better or more suitable than another choice, especially when two or more options are being compared
core_image: 天平两端各放一份方案，一端缓缓下沉，指针偏向那一边
scene: 两份方案摊在桌上，众人讨论到深夜，最后目光都落到右边那一份。 For a small team, a simple plan is usually preferable to a clever one.
sceneCN: 这里 preferable 是「更可取的」（第 1 个义项：两相比较中更值得选择）；句意为对小团队来说，简单的方案通常比巧妙的方案更可取。图中可辨识物件：桌面、两份方案、天平指针。

pos.zh: 更可取的；较好的；更合意的；更适宜的

derivatives.zh: 同一拉丁词干上的动词，经古法语 preferer 进入英语，义为「更喜欢；宁愿」
由 prefer 加名词后缀 -ence 构成，义为「偏爱；优先权」
由 preferable 加 -ly 构成，义为「最好；更合意地」

senses.title: Better when two things are compared
senses.definition: better or more suitable than the other option in a direct comparison
senses.definitionCN: 在两个选项直接比较时，比另一个更好或更合适
senses.example: A quiet room is preferable to a noisy one for study.
senses.exampleCN: 学习时，安静的房间比喧闹的房间更可取。
senses.why: Latin praeferre meant to carry one thing in front of another, so the adjective starts from a ranking in which one choice is set ahead of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praeferre 意为把一物抬到另一物前面，所以这个形容词的起点是排位：有一个选择被摆到了其余选择之前。

senses.title: More agreeable to a particular person
senses.definition: more to someone's liking, so that the person would choose it if left free to do so
senses.definitionCN: 更合乎某人的心意，若由他自由选择就会选它
senses.example: For her, an early flight is preferable to a late one.
senses.exampleCN: 对她来说，早班飞机比晚班飞机更合意。
senses.why: Preference is personal, so once the word ranks options it can also describe what one person happens to like better, not only what is better in general.
senses.whyCN: 偏爱是个人化的，所以这个词一旦用来给选项排位，也就能描述某个人恰好更喜欢什么，而不只是客观上什么更好。

senses.title: Wiser in the circumstances
senses.definition: more sensible or advisable in a particular situation, all things considered
senses.definitionCN: 通盘考虑之后，在特定情形里更明智、更值得采纳
senses.example: Given the ice on the road, walking is preferable to driving tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 考虑到路面结冰，今晚走路比开车更明智。
senses.why: When the circumstances are brought in, the comparison stops being a matter of taste and becomes a judgement about safety or good sense, which is how the word reaches advice.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把具体情形带进来，比较就不再是口味问题，而变成对安全与否、明智与否的判断，这个词也由此进入劝告的语境。

intro.en: Preferable joins a Latin prefix meaning before to a verb meaning to carry, and reached English through French as the adjective built on prefer.
intro.cn: preferable 把一个意为「在前」的拉丁前缀与一个意为「携带」的动词连在一起，经法语作为 prefer 的形容词进入英语。

items.en: The root behind Latin ferre is usually reconstructed as bher-, meaning to carry; it is a reconstructed form, not a word found in any text.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语 ferre 背后的词根可重构为 bher-，意为「携带」；这只是重构形式，并非任何文本中出现的词。

items.en: Ferre meant to bear or to carry, and it built a large family of verbs about bringing, holding and offering.
items.cn: ferre 意为承载、携带，由此造出一大批表示带来、持有与呈递的动词。

items.en: Prae- meant in front or before, so praeferre first meant to carry something in front, then to set one thing above another.
items.cn: prae- 意为在前面或之前，praeferre 先指把某物抬到前面，再引申为把一物置于另一物之上。

items.en: Old French kept the verb as preferer, meaning to put first or to value more, and formed the adjective preferable from it.
items.cn: 古法语把动词保留为 preferer，意为置于首位或更看重，并由它造出形容词 preferable。

items.en: English borrowed both prefer and preferable, and the adjective settled into the pattern preferable to, naming the better of two choices.
items.cn: 英语同时借入 prefer 与 preferable，这个形容词后来固定在 preferable to 的结构里，指两个选择中更好的那个。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin verb ferre; the near-meaning group gathers words that also rank one thing above another.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁动词 ferre 上的形式；近义组收同样把一物排在另一物之上的词。

entries.definition: To like one thing more than another and choose it.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的动词，义为更喜欢并选择某物。

entries.definition: The act of liking one thing more, or the thing that is liked more.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的名词，指偏爱这一行为，或所偏爱的事物。

entries.definition: If possible, as the more desirable choice.
entries.definitionCN: 由 preferable 加 -ly 构成，义为「最好；更合意地」。

entries.definition: Promotion to a higher position, from the older sense of being put forward.
entries.definitionCN: 由 prefer 加 -ment 构成，指晋升，来自「被推到前面」的旧义。

entries.definition: Of higher quality or more suitable than something else.
entries.definitionCN: 更好的；质量更高或更合适的。

entries.definition: Worth wanting or choosing because it brings an advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 值得向往的；因有好处而值得选择的。

entries.definition: Sensible and likely to bring a good result.
entries.definitionCN: 明智的；很可能带来好结果的。

entries.definition: Better than another thing of the same kind.
entries.definitionCN: 优于同类其他事物的；更好的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of carrying with a prefix meaning before, and its family keeps returning to ranking, liking and choosing.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是带「在前」前缀的拉丁「携带」动词，同族词反复回到排位、偏爱与选择。

normal.en: Praeferre is prae- plus ferre, to carry before, so to prefer is to put one thing ahead of another in your mind.
normal.cn: praeferre 是 prae- 加 ferre（携带），意为抬到前面，所以 to prefer 就是在心里把一物排到另一物之前。

normal.en: Preferable adds -able to the same stem, so it means worth being put first.
normal.cn: preferable 在同一词干后加 -able，意为「值得被放在前面的」。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is preferable to, not preferable than, because the Latin prefix already carries the comparison.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 preferable to 而不是 preferable than，因为比较的意思已由这个词本身承担。

normal.en: Preference is the noun of the same family, naming the state of liking one thing more.
normal.cn: preference 是同族名词，指更喜欢某物这种状态。

normal.en: Preferably is the adverb, used when a wish is stated politely rather than as an order.
normal.cn: preferably 是副词，用于客气地说出愿望，而不是下达命令。

abstract.en: To call something preferable is to admit that both options exist and that one has been weighed against the other.
abstract.cn: 说某物更可取，就是承认两个选项都存在，而且其中一个已经被拿来与另一个掂量过。

abstract.en: The word does not say the other choice is bad; it only says this one stands in front.
abstract.cn: 这个词并没有说另一个选择不好，只说这一个站到了前面。

abstract.en: Every preference is a small act of ordering the world, and the adjective names the result of that act.
abstract.cn: 每一次偏爱都是给世界排一次小序，这个形容词命名的正是排序的结果。

examples.en: For a small team, a simple plan is usually preferable to a clever one.
examples.cn: 对小团队来说，简单的方案通常比巧妙的方案更可取。

examples.en: Given the ice on the road, walking is preferable to driving tonight.
examples.cn: 考虑到路面结冰，今晚走路比开车更明智。

examples.en: Most parents find a short walk to school preferable to a long bus ride.
examples.cn: 多数家长觉得走一小段路去学校比坐长途公交更合意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偏爱若宝」——偏爱的东西总被当成宝贝放在最前面；preferable 就是更可取的。

root: 由拉丁语前缀 prae-（在前）与动词 ferre（携带）构成 praeferre（置于前面、更看重），经古法语 preferer 及形容词 preferable 进入英语；同族词有 prefer、preference、preferment。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a choice set in front of the others; the senses divide into an objective comparison, a personal liking, and a judgement about what is wise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被摆到其他选项之前的选择；义项由此分出客观比较、个人偏爱，以及对是否明智的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two plans on a scale, one side sinking slowly as the needle leans toward it.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两端各放一份方案，一端缓缓下沉，指针偏向那一边。

branches.en: a hand moving one sheet of paper to the top of a pile
branches.cn: 一只手把一张纸移到一叠纸的最上面

branches.en: a traveller choosing the earlier of two trains
branches.cn: 旅客在两班车中选了较早的一班

branches.en: a sign turning walkers away from an icy slope
branches.cn: 一块牌子让行人避开结冰的坡道

branches.en: two menus laid side by side on a table
branches.cn: 两份菜单并排摊在桌上

branches.en: a family voting on where to eat
branches.cn: 一家人投票决定去哪儿吃饭

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin prefix of place, a verb of carrying, and an English suffix meaning worth being chosen.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀、表示携带的动词，以及一个意为「值得被选」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Preferable rests on Latin praeferre, to carry before, built from prae- and ferre; French reshaped it into preferer and its adjective.
latinIntro.cn: preferable 立足于拉丁语 praeferre（抬到前面），由 prae- 与 ferre 构成；法语把它改写为 preferer 及其形容词。

items.meaning: to put first, to value more

definition_zh: 分别地；单独地；各自地
definition_en: in separate ways, one by one, or as distinct items
core_image: 两只盘子并排放着，各装各的食物，中间留着一道缝
scene: 两份报告被分别装进不同的信封。 The two reports were mailed separately.
sceneCN: 这里 separately 是「分别地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：两份报告被分别装进不同的信封。

senses.title: In separate ways
senses.definition: in ways that are not together
senses.definitionCN: 以不在一起的方式
senses.example: The two reports were mailed separately.
senses.exampleCN: 两份报告被分别装进不同的信封。
senses.why: This is the basic adverb sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的副词义。

senses.title: One by one
senses.definition: one at a time rather than as a group
senses.definitionCN: 一次一个而非作为整体
senses.example: Each student was tested separately.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生都单独接受了测试。
senses.why: Being apart also means being counted alone.
senses.whyCN: 分开也意味着被单独计数。

intro.en: Separately is separate plus -ly, from Latin separare, to set apart.
intro.cn: separately 由 separate 加 -ly 构成，源自拉丁语 separare（使分开）。

items.en: Separare meant to set apart.
items.cn: separare 意为使分开。

items.en: Separate entered English as adjective and verb.
items.cn: separate 作为形容词与动词进入英语。

items.en: The adverb added -ly to the adjective.
items.cn: 副词在形容词后加 -ly 构成。

items.en: Separately marks actions done apart.
items.cn: separately 标记分开完成的动作。

items.en: It often appears on price lists.
items.cn: 它常出现在价目表上。

note.en: Separately is compared with similar-looking words and with words for doing things apart.
note.cn: 把 separately 与形近词以及表示分开行事的词作比较。

the act of dividing
able to be divided
one by one
without relying on others
separated by distance

normalIntro.en: Separately tells us that things are handled one apart from another.
normalIntro.cn: separately 表示事物彼此分开处理。

normal.en: The adverb is formed with -ly.
normal.cn: 这个副词由 -ly 构成。

normal.en: Shipping is charged separately.
normal.cn: 运费另行收取。

normal.en: They arrived separately.
normal.cn: 他们各自到达。

normal.en: Test the samples separately.
normal.cn: 分别测试这些样本。

normal.en: Sold separately means not included.
normal.cn: sold separately 意为不包含在内。

abstract.en: Counting things apart is the first step to comparing them.
abstract.cn: 把事物分开计数，是比较它们的第一步。

abstract.en: Two paths can run parallel without touching.
abstract.cn: 两条路可以平行而不相交。

abstract.en: Sometimes being separate is what keeps a bond intact.
abstract.cn: 有时分开反而让纽带保持完好。

examples.en: The two reports were mailed separately.
examples.cn: 两份报告被分别装进不同的信封。

examples.en: Each student was tested separately.
examples.cn: 每个学生都单独接受了测试。

examples.en: The parts are sold separately.

dict_mnemonic.text: separately 是 separate（分开的）加 -ly 构成的副词，表示「分别地、各自地」。

root: 由 separate（分开的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，核心义「以分开的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Separately means in separate ways or one by one.
sensesIntro.cn: separately 意为分别地或逐个地。

core.en: Actions done apart from one another.

branches.en: Things handled in different places.
branches.cn: 在不同地方处理的事物。

branches.en: People counted one at a time.
branches.cn: 被逐个计数的人。

branches.en: Apartness applies to groups and individuals.
branches.cn: 分开既可指群体也可指个体。

branches.en: Costs are listed on their own.
branches.cn: 费用被单独列出。

branches.en: Each result stands by itself.
branches.cn: 每个结果各自成立。

intro.en: Separately belongs to the Latin separare family.
intro.cn: separately 属于拉丁语 separare（使分开）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin separare is the historical base of the whole family.

definition_zh: 冒犯的；无礼的；令人反感的；进攻的；攻势
definition_en: causing someone to feel insulted or upset; extremely unpleasant; used for or taking the attack; as a noun, a planned military attack
core_image: 一句话和一支军队都朝着同一个方向推出去
scene: 看台上有人拉起一条嘲弄对方球队的横幅，周围的笑声很快变成了争吵。 The referee warned that the banner was offensive and had to be removed.
sceneCN: 这里 offensive 是「冒犯的、无礼的」（第 1 个义项：使人感到被冒犯）；句意是裁判警告那条横幅带有冒犯意味，必须撤下。画面里有看台、横幅和争执的观众。

pos.zh: 冒犯的；无礼的；令人反感的；进攻的

derivatives.zh: 由 offensive 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「冒犯地；进攻性地」
由 offensive 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「冒犯性；令人反感的程度」
由同一拉丁词干 offensa 构成，义为「罪行；冒犯」（英式拼写）
由表示「反」的 counter- 与 offensive 复合而成，义为「反攻」

senses.title: Causing someone to feel insulted
senses.definition: causing someone to feel hurt, angry or insulted
senses.definitionCN: 使别人感到受伤、恼火或受辱的
senses.example: His remarks about her accent were offensive.
senses.exampleCN: 他关于她口音的那些话很冒犯人。
senses.why: The suffix -ive turns the act of striking against into a quality, so words and acts that wound people are called offensive.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 把「撞上去」这个动作变成一种性质，于是会伤人的话和行为就被称作冒犯的。

senses.title: Extremely unpleasant to the senses
senses.definition: very unpleasant, especially to see, smell or hear
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在视觉、嗅觉或听觉上非常令人不适的
senses.example: The smell from the drains was offensive.
senses.exampleCN: 下水道里传来的气味很难闻。
senses.why: The blow can land on the senses as well as on feelings, so the adjective also grades what makes the eyes, nose or ears recoil.
senses.whyCN: 这一击不只落在感情上，也落在感官上，所以这个形容词也能形容让眼睛、鼻子或耳朵想要后退的东西。

senses.title: Used for attack; attacking
senses.definition: designed or used for attacking, especially in war or sport
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在战争或体育中为进攻而设计或使用的
senses.example: The soldiers were trained to use offensive weapons.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们受过使用攻击性武器的训练。
senses.why: Because offendere pictured a blow aimed forward, the adjective also names whatever is built to push into the enemy's ground.
senses.whyCN: 因为 offendere 的意象是朝前打出的一击，这个形容词也就用来指一切为推进到对方阵地而准备的东西。

senses.title: A planned military attack
senses.definition: a large organized military attack, or a spell of attacking in a game
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的大规模军事进攻，或比赛中一段持续进攻
senses.example: The spring offensive opened along the whole front.
senses.exampleCN: 春季攻势在整条战线上展开。
senses.why: When the adjective names the attacking mode, it can stand as a noun for the attack itself, so the quality becomes the campaign.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词用来指进攻的方式，它就能独立成名词指进攻本身，性质于是变成了一场战役。

intro.en: Offensive is an adjective built on a Latin participle stem, and it split in English into the insulting, the disgusting and the attacking.
intro.cn: offensive 是建立在拉丁语过去分词词干上的形容词，在英语里分出「冒犯」「令人反感」与「进攻」三路。

items.en: The verb offendere meant to strike against, and its participle stem offens- carried the idea of something that has hit a target.
items.cn: 动词 offendere 意为撞上，其过去分词词干 offens- 带着「已经击中目标」的意思。

items.en: Medieval Latin offensivus, commonly derived from that stem, meant hurtful or ready to strike.
items.cn: 一般认为中世纪拉丁语 offensivus 由这个词干构成，意为会伤人的、动辄要打的。

items.en: Old French offensif took the adjective into French and passed it on to English with the sense of hurtful and attacking.
items.cn: 古法语 offensif 把这个形容词接了过去，再传入英语，带着「会伤人」与「用于进攻」两层意思。

items.en: In English the adjective grew two branches, one for insulting words and one for weapons, and the noun later named a military push.
items.cn: 在英语里这个形容词长出两支，一支指无礼的话，一支指武器，名词后来则用来指一次军事推进。

items.en: Modern English uses offensive for rude remarks, for disgusting smells, and for the attacking side in war and sport.
items.cn: 现代英语用 offensive 指无礼的话、恶心的气味，以及战争与体育中进攻的一方。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun and verb behind this adjective; the near-meaning group gathers words for insult, disgust and attack.
note.cn: 形近组收这个形容词背后的名词与动词；近义组收表示侮辱、反感与进攻的词。

entries.definition: The noun for a crime or an insult, from the same Latin stem.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词干上表示罪行或冒犯的名词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the noun from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上名词的美式拼写。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to insult someone or to break a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 表示冒犯他人或违反规则的动词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in an insulting or attacking way.
entries.definitionCN: 表示以冒犯或进攻的方式的副词。

entries.definition: Rude and likely to humiliate the person addressed.
entries.definitionCN: 粗鲁并可能使对方受辱的。

entries.definition: Showing little respect for other people.
So unpleasant that it causes strong dislike.
A planned attempt to defeat an enemy or an opponent.
entries.definitionCN: 为击败敌人或对手而计划发动的进攻。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin stem for striking, and it keeps the same forward push whether the target is a person, a nose or an army.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示打击的拉丁词干上，无论目标是个人、鼻子还是一支军队，它都保持同一个向前的推力。

normal.en: Offend plus -ive makes a quality: what is offensive has the habit of striking people.
normal.cn: offend 加 -ive 构成一种性质：会冒犯的东西带着「打到人」的习性。

normal.en: The same adjective serves for rude remarks and for attacking weapons, because both push forward.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词既修饰无礼的话，也修饰进攻的武器，因为两者都朝前推。

normal.en: Take the offensive turns the adjective into a noun phrase for going on the attack.
normal.cn: take the offensive 把形容词变成名词性短语，表示转为进攻。

normal.en: Offensiveness adds -ness to the adjective and names the quality itself.
normal.cn: offensiveness 在形容词后加 -ness，直接指这种性质本身。

normal.en: Offensive weapon is a legal phrase for something built or used to hurt people.
normal.cn: offensive weapon 是法律用语，指为伤人而制作或使用的物件。

abstract.en: A rude sentence and an advancing army share one direction: both are pushed outward, and both make people step back.
abstract.cn: 一句无礼的话与一支推进的军队共享一个方向：都向外推，也都让人后退。

abstract.en: Offensive smell arrives before words do; the nose is hit before anyone has spoken.
abstract.cn: 令人反感的气味先于语言到达；还没人开口，鼻子已经被击中。

abstract.en: The suffix -ive turns a blow into a tendency, a readiness to keep pushing against whatever is in front.
abstract.cn: 后缀 -ive 把一次打击变成一种倾向，一种不断朝前方顶撞的劲头。

examples.en: His remarks about her accent were offensive.
examples.cn: 他关于她口音的那些话很冒犯人。

examples.en: The smell from the drains was offensive.
examples.cn: 下水道里传来的气味很难闻。

examples.en: The spring offensive opened along the whole front.
examples.cn: 春季攻势在整条战线上展开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，芬西服」——哦，那套芬兰西服穿得怪，让人反感；offensive 就是冒犯的、进攻的。

root: 拉丁语 offendere（撞上、触犯）的过去分词词干 offens- 加 -ive 构成 offensivus，经古法语 offensif 进入英语；同一词干还生出 offence 与 offend。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the forward push of a blow; the adjective splits into insult, disgust and attack, and the noun names the attack itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一击向前的推力」；形容词分出冒犯、反感与进攻，名词则指进攻本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence and an army pushing out in the same direction.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话与一支军队朝同一个方向推出去。

branches.en: a mocking remark about someone's accent
branches.cn: 一句拿别人口音取笑的话

branches.en: a smell by the rubbish bins that stops conversation
branches.cn: 垃圾桶边的气味让人停住话头

branches.en: a weapon built only for hurting people
branches.cn: 只为伤人而制造的武器

branches.en: an attack opened in spring across a long front
branches.cn: 春天在漫长战线上发起的进攻

branches.en: one force that makes people step back, in words or in air
branches.cn: 同一种让人后退的力量，或在言语，或在空气里

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb of striking, its participle stem, and an adjectival suffix that turns the act into a lasting quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示打击的拉丁动词、它的过去分词词干，以及把动作变成持久性质的后缀共同构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: having the nature of, tending to
in an insulting or attacking way

items.meaningCN: 构成表示性质的抽象名词

definition_zh: 有利的；赞同的；讨人喜欢的
definition_en: helpful or advantageous, showing approval, or giving a good impression
core_image: 帆船离岸那天风向正好，船头轻轻切开平静的海面
scene: 天气预报说风向合适，正是出海的好日子。 The weather was favourable for sailing.
sceneCN: 这里 favourable 是「有利的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：天气对航行有利。

pos.zh: 讨人喜欢的；给人好印象的

senses.title: Helpful or advantageous
senses.definition: making success more likely or conditions better
senses.definitionCN: 使成功更有可能或使条件更好
senses.example: The conditions were favourable for an early start.
senses.exampleCN: 条件有利于尽早出发。
senses.why: This is the main sense in weather and planning.
senses.whyCN: 这是天气与计划语境中的主要含义。

senses.title: Showing approval
senses.definition: expressing a positive opinion or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 表达正面看法或同意
senses.example: The committee gave a favourable response.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会给出了赞同的回应。
senses.why: A favourable reply carries approval.
senses.whyCN: favourable 的答复意味着赞同。

senses.title: Giving a good impression
senses.titleCN: 讨人喜欢的；给人好印象的
senses.definition: pleasing and likely to create a good opinion
senses.definitionCN: 令人满意、容易赢得良好评价的
senses.example: She made a favourable impression on the panel.
senses.exampleCN: 她给评审组留下了好印象。
senses.why: The sense moves from useful conditions to pleasing qualities.
senses.whyCN: 该义从有利条件转向讨人喜欢的品质。

intro.en: Favourable comes from Latin favorabilis, through Old French favorable.
intro.cn: favourable 源自拉丁语 favorabilis，经古法语 favorable 传入英语。

items.en: Favorabilis meant deserving or showing favor.
items.cn: favorabilis 意为值得青睐或表示好意的。

items.en: Favorable described something kind or helpful.
items.cn: favorable 形容善意或有利的事物。

items.en: The word entered English as a term for helpful conditions.
items.cn: 该词以「有利条件」之义进入英语。

items.en: British spelling settled as favourable with a u.
items.cn: 英式拼写固定为带 u 的 favourable。

items.en: The word now also describes approving replies and good impressions.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词也形容赞同的答复与良好印象。

note.en: Favourable is compared with similar-looking words and with words for advantage.
note.cn: 把 favourable 与形近词以及表示有利的词作比较。

entries.definition: the American spelling of favourable
liked best
in a helpful or approving way
giving an advantage
hopeful and constructive
giving useful help

normalIntro.en: Favourable describes conditions that help, replies that approve, and qualities that please.
normalIntro.cn: favourable 形容有利的条件、赞同的答复与讨人喜欢的品质。

normal.en: Favourable weather makes a voyage easier.
normal.cn: 有利的天气让航行更轻松。

normal.en: A favourable reply says yes in a polite way.
normal.cn: favourable 的答复是以礼貌方式表示同意。

normal.en: A favourable impression often opens a door.
normal.cn: 好印象常常能打开一扇门。

normal.en: The opposite is unfavourable, with un- at the front.
normal.cn: 反义词是 unfavourable，在前面加 un-。

normal.en: American English drops the u and writes favorable.
normal.cn: 美式英语去掉 u，写作 favorable。

abstract.en: A wind can be favourable without being gentle.
abstract.cn: 有利的风未必是温和的风。

abstract.en: Conditions and opinions share one word because both can help or block.
abstract.cn: 条件与意见共用一个词，因为两者都能助人也能阻碍。

abstract.en: What pleases the eye is also what wins approval.
abstract.cn: 悦目之物也容易赢得赞同。

examples.en: The conditions were favourable for an early start.
examples.cn: 条件有利于尽早出发。

examples.en: She made a favourable impression on the panel.
examples.cn: 她给评审组留下了好印象。

examples.en: The reply was favourable and the deal went ahead.
examples.cn: 答复是赞同的，交易继续进行。

dict_mnemonic.text: favourable 由 favour 加 -able 构成，字面是「能带来好意的」，引申为「有利的、赞同的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 favorabilis（值得青睐的），经古法语 favorable，核心义「能带来帮助与好感的」。

sensesIntro.en: Favourable means helpful, approving, or pleasing enough to create a good impression.
sensesIntro.cn: favourable 意为有利的、赞同的，或讨人喜欢、能留下好印象的。

core.en: Something that works in your favour, whether conditions, replies, or looks.
core.cn: 对你有益的事物，无论是条件、答复还是外表。

branches.en: Conditions that make success easier.
branches.cn: 让成功更容易的条件。

branches.en: A response that shows agreement.
branches.cn: 表示同意的回应。

branches.en: A quality that wins a good opinion.
branches.cn: 赢得良好评价的品质。

branches.en: Both good weather and a good manner help you forward.
branches.cn: 好天气与好举止都有助于你前进。

branches.en: Helpful conditions and approving people often arrive together.
branches.cn: 有利条件与赞同的人常常一起出现。

intro.en: Favourable forms words for advantage, approval, and their opposites.
intro.cn: favourable 构成表示有利、赞同及其反面的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin favorabilis and favere are the historical sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 favorabilis 与 favere 是历史来源。

items.example: He asked for a small favour.
They judged the favourableness of the soil.
items.exampleCN: 他们评估了土壤的适宜程度。

items.example: The ship waited out unfavourable winds.
The report compared the two plans unfavourably.
items.exampleCN: 报告把两个计划作了不利的比较。
蓝色是她最喜欢的颜色。
受青睐的候选人获胜了。

items.example: A favouring bias spoiled the test.
items.exampleCN: 偏袒倾向破坏了测试的公正。

definition_zh: 准时的；守时的；按时的；（术语）点的，点状的
definition_en: arriving or happening at the agreed time, and, in technical use, relating to a single point
core_image: 站台上的钟走到约定那一分，一个人正好踏进车门
scene: 清晨的站台上，列车还没停稳，一个提着公文包的人已经站在黄线后看表。 She is always punctual, reaching the office before anyone else.
sceneCN: 这里取「准时的」（第 1 个义项：人按约定时间到达）；句意是她总是很准时，比谁都先到办公室。黄线后看表的人影就是线索。

pos.zh: 准时的；守时的；按时的；（术语）点的

derivatives.zh: 由 punctual 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「准时地；按时地」
由 punctual 加名词后缀 -ity（源自拉丁 -itas）构成，义为「守时；准时」
由否定前缀 un- 加 punctual 构成，义为「不准时的；常迟到的」

senses.title: Arriving at the agreed time
senses.definition: of a person, arriving at the time that was agreed or arranged
senses.definitionCN: 指人按约定或安排好的时间到达
senses.example: The teacher is punctual and never keeps a class waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老师很守时，从不让全班等她。
senses.why: The word began as punctualis, 'relating to a point', and a fixed hour is exactly a point on the clock that a person chooses to land on.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初写作 punctualis，意思是「与点有关的」；约定的那个钟点正是时间上的一个「点」，守时的人就是让自己的到达落在这个点上。

senses.title: Happening at the fixed hour
senses.definition: of an event or arrangement, starting or taking place at the exact time set
senses.definitionCN: 指事件或安排在其设定的准确时刻开始或发生
senses.example: The punctual start of the ceremony surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 典礼准点开始，让所有人都感到意外。
senses.why: If one person can land on the point of an hour, so can a ceremony; the same picture moves from a single arrival to the timing of a whole event.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个人可以落在钟点这个「点」上，一场典礼也可以；同一个画面从单个人的到达，扩大为整场活动的时间安排。

senses.title: Done without delay
senses.definition: of an action such as payment or reply, done at the time it was promised
senses.definitionCN: 指付款、回复等行为在承诺的时间完成
senses.example: Punctual payment of the rent keeps the contract in good standing.
senses.exampleCN: 按时交房租能让合同保持有效。
senses.why: The point on the clock is also a deadline; when the action lands on it, the habit of being on time becomes a quality of the act itself.
senses.whyCN: 钟点上的那个点同时也是一条期限；当行为正好落在这个点上，「守时」就从人的习惯变成了行为本身的属性。

senses.title: (Technical) belonging to a point
senses.definition: in technical writing, existing at or relating to a single point rather than to an area
senses.definitionCN: 在技术性文字中，指存在于某一点上或与单点有关的，而不是涉及一个面
senses.example: The model treats each charge as punctual, with no size at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型把每个电荷都当作点来处理，完全不考虑其大小。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer, kept almost unchanged: punctum is a point made by a prick, so the adjective still says 'of a point' before it ever says 'on time'.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层，几乎没有改变：punctum 是被刺出来的一个点，所以这个形容词最早说的就是「关于点的」，后来才说「准时的」。

intro.en: Punctual goes back to the Latin verb for pricking, whose noun punctum means a point; the modern sense of keeping time grew out of landing exactly on a point of the clock.
intro.cn: punctual 可追到拉丁语中表示「刺」的动词，其名词 punctum 意为「点」；现代「守时」义正是从「落在钟面的某一点上」长出来的。

items.en: Pungere meant to prick or to pierce, and it is the physical act behind the whole family.
items.cn: pungere 意为刺、扎，是整族词背后那个具体的动作。

items.en: A punctum was the small mark left by a prick, and from that it came to mean a point in space or in writing.
items.cn: punctum 是刺一下留下的小痕，由此指空间或文字中的一个点。

items.en: Medieval Latin punctualis meant relating to a point and was used for things fixed to one exact point.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 punctualis 意为「与点有关的」，用于指固定在某一确切点上的事物。

items.en: English took the adjective in the seventeenth century, first in the technical sense and then for keeping to an appointed hour.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，先用其技术义，随后用来指遵守约定的钟点。

items.en: Modern English uses punctual almost only for people and events that keep time, while the older sense survives in technical writing.
items.cn: 现代英语几乎只用 punctual 指守时的人和准点的事，较古的「点的」义则保留在技术文字里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of pricking and its noun for a point; the near-meaning group gathers words for keeping to time.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「刺」动词及其「点」名词上的词；近义组收表示遵守时间的词。

entries.definition: The marks that divide writing, named from the same Latin word for a point.
entries.definitionCN: 标点符号，名字来自同一个表示「点」的拉丁词。

entries.definition: A small hole made by something sharp.
Sharp in taste or smell, as if pricking the nose.
entries.definitionCN: 味道或气味刺激的，像扎鼻子一样。

entries.definition: Extremely careful about the small details of behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 对行为细节极为讲究的。

entries.definition: Done at once, without delay.
Happening at a good or useful moment.
entries.definitionCN: 发生在合适或有用时机的。

entries.definition: Happening at the same times and in the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 按时、按固定方式发生的。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from a dot pricked into a surface, and its family keeps returning to points and to the hours that people agree on.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从刺在表面上的一个小点开始，同族词反复回到「点」以及人们约定的小时。

normal.en: Pungere means to prick and punctum is the dot left by the prick, so the word starts from a single point.
normal.cn: pungere 意为刺，punctum 是刺出来的那个小点，所以这个词的起点是一个「点」。

normal.en: The hour you agree on is a point on the clock, and a punctual person lands exactly on it.
normal.cn: 约定的小时是钟面上的一个点，守时的人正好让到达落在这个点上。

normal.en: Punctuality is built with -ity, and it names the habit rather than one arrival.
normal.cn: punctuality 加 -ity 构成名词，指这种习惯，而不是某一次到达。

normal.en: Punctually adds -ly and describes the way an action is carried out.
normal.cn: punctually 加 -ly，用来说明动作是怎样完成的。

normal.en: Punctuation and puncture share the same point: one marks a page, the other marks a surface.
normal.cn: punctuation 与 puncture 共享同一个「点」：一个点在纸面上，一个扎在物体表面。

abstract.en: Being on time is a small promise kept, which is how a word for a dot became a word about trust.
abstract.cn: 守时是一个被兑现的小承诺，那个表示「点」的词就这样变成了关于信任的词。

abstract.en: A clock turns time into points, and every appointment is a point two people agree to meet at.
abstract.cn: 钟把时间变成一个个点，每一次约会就是两个人约定相见的一个点。

abstract.en: The distance between almost and exactly is the whole subject of this word.
abstract.cn: 「差一点」与「正好」之间的距离，正是这个词的全部主题。

examples.en: The teacher is punctual and never keeps a class waiting.
examples.cn: 这位老师很守时，从不让全班等她。

examples.en: Punctual payment of the rent keeps the contract in good standing.
examples.cn: 按时交房租能让合同保持有效。

examples.en: The punctual start of the ceremony surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 典礼准点开始，让所有人都感到意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近「碰克秋」——听着像「碰巧赶上」，正好在那一点赶到，就是准时。

root: 拉丁语 pungere（刺）→ punctum（刺出的小点）→ 中世纪拉丁语 punctualis（与点有关的），十七世纪进入英语，由「落在某一点上」发展出「守时」义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is landing on a single point of time; the senses divide into a person who arrives, an event that begins, an action done on time, and the old technical sense of a point.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「落在时间的某一个点上」；义项分成到达的人、开始的事、按时完成的行为，以及古老的「点」这一术语义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a station clock reaching the agreed minute as a traveller steps through the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：站台上的钟走到约定的那一分，一个旅人正好踏进车门。

branches.en: a commuter standing behind the yellow line, checking the time
branches.cn: 通勤者站在黄线后看表

branches.en: a ceremony beginning as the clock ticks the hour
branches.cn: 钟声敲响时开始的典礼

branches.en: rent paid on the first day of the month
branches.cn: 每月第一天付掉的房租

branches.en: a diagram where every charge is reduced to a dot
branches.cn: 把每个电荷都简化成一个点的示意图

branches.en: a person and a payment both landing on the agreed minute
branches.cn: 人与一笔钱都落在约定的那一刻

intro.en: A Latin verb of pricking and its noun for a point hold the word together, and Latin and English endings build the adjective, the adverb and the two nouns.
intro.cn: 表示「刺」的拉丁语动词及其「点」名词共同支撑这个词，拉丁语与英语的词尾再构成形容词、副词和两个名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pungere, to prick, punctum, a point, and the Medieval Latin adjective punctualis are the direct sources of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pungere（刺）、punctum（点）与中世纪拉丁语形容词 punctualis 是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.meaning: on time, relating to a point
the habit of being on time

definition_zh: 神庙；寺庙；圣殿；太阳穴；眼镜腿；（文化）殿堂
definition_en: a building used for worship in many religions, or the flat side of the forehead above the cheekbone
core_image: 石柱围出一间内殿，门内是神像，门外是台阶；同一张脸上，眉骨外侧的一处凹陷也叫这个名字
scene: 山道尽头是石阶与断柱，海风穿过柱间。 The temple stands on the ridge above the harbour, its columns still unbroken.
sceneCN: 这里 temple 指「供奉神明的神庙」（第 1 个义项：古代宗教建筑）；句意为这座神庙立在海港上方的山脊上，柱身至今未断。图中可辨识物件：石阶、断柱、山脊、海港。

senses.title: A shrine of the old religions
senses.definition: a building dedicated to a god, especially in Greek, Roman or Egyptian worship
senses.definitionCN: 献给某位神明的建筑，尤见于希腊、罗马或埃及崇拜
senses.example: The temple walls still carry the names of donors from three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 神庙墙上仍留着三个世纪以来捐赠者的名字。
senses.why: the oldest sense is a marked-off sacred precinct, and the building is only its most visible part.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是一块被划分出来的神圣地界，建筑只是它最显眼的部分。

senses.title: An East Asian place of worship
senses.definition: a Buddhist, Taoist or Shinto building used for worship and ritual
senses.definitionCN: 佛教、道教或神道用于礼拜与仪式的建筑
senses.example: Incense smoke hangs under the temple eaves all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午，香烟都悬在寺庙的檐下。
senses.why: the word travelled with traders and translators, so it was applied to buildings of religions it never originally named.
senses.whyCN: 这个词随商人与译者旅行，于是被用在它原本从未命名的宗教建筑上。

senses.title: The Temple of Jerusalem
senses.definition: the central sanctuary of ancient Israel, of which only the western retaining wall survives
senses.definitionCN: 古代以色列的中心圣所，今仅存西侧挡土墙
senses.example: Pilgrims still pray at the wall of the temple.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者仍在圣殿的墙边祈祷。
senses.why: in this use the word is almost a proper name: one building, one city, one covenant.
senses.whyCN: 在这一用法中，这个词几乎成了专名：一座建筑、一座城、一份盟约。

senses.title: A Latter-day Saint temple
senses.definition: a building in the Latter-day Saint movement reserved for special ordinances, as distinct from an ordinary meetinghouse
senses.definitionCN: 后期圣徒运动中专供特定仪式的建筑，区别于普通礼拜堂
senses.example: Only members with recommends enter the temple for ordinances.
senses.exampleCN: 只有持推荐书的成员才能进圣殿参加仪式。
senses.why: a new religion kept the old word but narrowed it to one kind of building among several.
senses.whyCN: 一个新宗教沿用了旧词，却把它收窄为若干建筑中的一类。

senses.title: The side of the forehead
senses.definition: the flat area at the side of the forehead above the cheekbone
senses.definitionCN: 额部两侧、颧骨上方的平坦区域
senses.example: The blow landed on his left temple and blurred his vision.
senses.exampleCN: 那一击打在他左侧太阳穴，令视线发花。
senses.why: this is a different Latin word, the plural of the time noun, which in the plural named the temples of the head.
senses.whyCN: 这是另一个拉丁词，即「时间」名词的复数形式，其复数专门指头部的太阳穴。

senses.title: The arm of a pair of glasses
senses.definition: the part of a spectacle frame that rests against the side of the head
senses.definitionCN: 眼镜架上贴着头部两侧的部分
senses.example: One temple of the frame was bent after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 摔倒之后，镜架的一条腿弯了。
senses.why: eyeglasses are named by the body part they touch, so the anatomical word was transferred to the frame.
senses.whyCN: 眼镜以它所接触的身体部位命名，因此这个解剖词被转用到镜架上。

senses.title: A temple of art or commerce
senses.definition: a large building devoted to a valued activity, described with religious awe
senses.definitionCN: 把某项受珍视的活动说成带有宗教敬畏的大型建筑
senses.example: The old library is a temple of quiet and paper.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老图书馆是一座安静与纸张的殿堂。
senses.why: the metaphor works because both a temple and a great hall set apart a space from ordinary use.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，因为神庙与宏伟厅堂都把一处空间从日常使用中划分出来。

senses.title: A marked-off piece of sky
senses.titleCN: 古罗马占卜划定的天空区
senses.definition: in Roman augury, a region of the sky marked out for observing signs
senses.definitionCN: 罗马占卜中为观察征兆而划出的一片天空区域
senses.example: The augur divided the temple of the sky into quarters.
senses.exampleCN: 占卜官把这片天空的圣域分成四方。
senses.why: the Latin word began as a space cut off for observation, which is why the building sense and the sky sense share a root.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词最初是为观察而划出的一片空间，因此建筑义与天空义共用同一词根。

intro.en: Two different Latin words lie behind English temple: one means a consecrated space, the other names the temples of the head. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 英语 temple 背后有两个不同的拉丁词：一个指被祝圣的空间，另一个指头部的太阳穴。年代均为约数。

items.en: Templum meant a space marked out and consecrated for observation, especially by an augur, and only later a shrine building.
items.cn: templum 指划出并祝圣供观察的空间，尤用于占卜，后来才指神庙建筑。

items.en: English borrowed the word early, and it appears in Old English for the Temple of Jerusalem before it named pagan shrines.
items.cn: 英语很早就借入这个词，古英语中先用于指耶路撒冷圣殿，之后才指异教神庙。

items.en: The plural of the time noun, tempora, was used for the flat places at either side of the forehead, giving the anatomical sense.
items.cn: 表示「时间」的名词其复数 tempora 被用来指额头两侧的平坦处，形成解剖义。

items.en: Translators extended the word to Buddhist and Taoist buildings, so English temple now covers many religions.
items.cn: 译者把这个词扩展到佛教与道教建筑，因此英语 temple 如今涵盖多种宗教。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the anatomical word named the side pieces of eyeglasses, which rest against the temples.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个解剖词被用来命名眼镜架两侧贴着太阳穴的部分。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the ancestry of templum before Latin is not established; a link to a verb meaning 'to cut' has been proposed, but competing explanations exist and none is proven.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：templum 在拉丁语之前的谱系未得到证明；有人提出它与表示「切」的动词有关，但存在多种竞争性解释，无一得到证实。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like temple or sit in the same semantic field but differ in root; group two holds other sacred buildings.
note.cn: 第一组是与 temple 形近或同属语义场、但词根不同的词；第二组是其他宗教建筑。

entries.definition: A small pattern or gauge used in building; it comes from the same root as template and has nothing to do with worship.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑中用的小样板或规尺，与 template 同源，与礼拜无关。

entries.definition: Relating to time or the material world; it comes from the time noun, which also supplied the plural behind the anatomical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 与时间或世俗世界相关的；来自「时间」名词，该名词的复数又给出了解剖义。

entries.definition: To look at or think about at length; it comes from the Latin verb for observing within a marked-off space.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间注视或思考；来自拉丁语中「在被划出的空间内观察」的动词。

entries.definition: The speed of music, from Italian tempo 'time'; it shares the Latin time noun but not the shrine word.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐的速度，来自意大利语「时间」；与拉丁「时间」名词同源，但与神庙词无关。

entries.definition: A place or receptacle holding something holy, often smaller than a temple and centred on a relic.
entries.definitionCN: 存放圣物之处或容器，常比神庙小，并以圣物为中心。

entries.definition: The holiest room of a religious building or a place of refuge; it stresses protection.
entries.definitionCN: 宗教建筑中最神圣的房间或避难处；强调保护。

entries.definition: A building for Christian worship; temple is used for other traditions and for the Jewish sanctuary.
entries.definitionCN: 基督教礼拜建筑；temple 多用于其他传统或犹太圣所。

entries.definition: A Jewish house of prayer and study; the Temple was the single sanctuary, while synagogues are local.
entries.definitionCN: 犹太人的祈祷与研习之所；圣殿是唯一圣所，会堂则是地方性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real Latin sources, the real translation history and the real glasses term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的拉丁语来源、真实的翻译史与真实的眼镜术语。

normal.en: The building sense means a space marked off for a god; the head sense means the flat side of the forehead.
normal.cn: 建筑义指为神划出的空间；头部义指额侧的平坦处。

normal.en: The family runs temple, temples, temple-like, templed, contemplate, contemplation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 temple、temples、temple-like、templed、contemplate、contemplation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: Buddhist temple, temple ruins, the Temple in Jerusalem, temple of art.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：佛寺、神庙遗址、耶路撒冷圣殿、艺术殿堂。

normal.en: The glasses sense is anatomy transferred to an object that touches the same spot.
normal.cn: 眼镜义是把解剖词转用到接触同一部位的物件上。

normal.en: Roman augury used the word for a patch of sky before it was used for a building.
normal.cn: 罗马占卜先用这个词指一片天空，之后才用于建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a rope laid on the ground to mark a square of sky as belonging to a god.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子铺在地上，把一方天空划归某位神明。

abstract.en: Picture a forehead and a temple wall both carrying the same small hollow.
abstract.cn: 想象额头与神庙的墙各有一处相同的小凹。

abstract.en: Picture a library so silent that visitors whisper as if at an altar.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆静得让访客像在祭坛前一样低语。

examples.en: The temple was rebuilt in marble after the earthquake.
examples.cn: 地震之后，这座神庙用大理石重建。

examples.en: A small temple stands at the top of the stone stair.
examples.cn: 石阶顶端立着一座小寺庙。

examples.en: The frame's temple snapped where it met the hinge.
examples.cn: 镜架的那条腿在铰链处折断了。

dict_mnemonic.text: templum（划出的神圣空间）→ 神庙；同形词又指额侧平坦处 → 太阳穴

root: 建筑义来自拉丁 templum「划出并祝圣的空间」，后指神庙；太阳穴义来自拉丁 tempora，即「时间」名词的复数，专指额侧；两源不同。英语 temple。templum 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow two paths: a marked-off sacred space becomes a shrine, then a whole class of religious buildings and a metaphor; a separate Latin plural names the forehead, then the glasses arm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分两条线：被划出的神圣空间成为神庙，再扩展为各类宗教建筑与比喻；另一个拉丁复数指额侧，再转指眼镜腿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary drawn around a space, and a hollow at the side of a face that shares the same name.
core.cn: 核心意象：围绕一处空间画下的界线，以及脸侧一处同名的凹陷。

branches.en: MARKED-OFF SPACE: the shrine and the augur's patch of sky are the same act of setting space apart.
branches.cn: 划出的空间：神庙与占卜官划出的那片天空，是同一个「把空间分开」的动作。

branches.en: MANY FAITHS: translation and new religions apply the word to their own buildings.
branches.cn: 多种信仰：翻译与新宗教把这个词用于自己的建筑。

branches.en: THE UNIQUE SANCTUARY: one building becomes a proper name and a whole covenant.
branches.cn: 唯一的圣所：一座建筑成为专名，也代表一整份盟约。

branches.en: THE FOREHEAD: a separate Latin plural names the head, and glasses borrow it.
branches.cn: 额侧：另一个拉丁复数指头部，眼镜又把它借去。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any revered place can be called a temple of its own craft.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何受敬重的地方都可称为其本行的殿堂。

intro.en: Temple is two words in one shape: a Latin sacred-space noun and a Latin plural for the sides of the head, so the affix list follows both.
intro.cn: temple 是一个词形下的两个词：一个拉丁语「神圣空间」名词与一个指头侧的拉丁语复数，因此词缀清单两条线都跟。

latinIntro.en: Latin templum gave the shrine family, and the plural tempora gave the anatomical family; the verb contemplari grew from templum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 templum 给出神庙一族，复数 tempora 给出解剖一族；动词 contemplari 由 templum 生长出来。

items.example: The augur observed within the templum.
items.exampleCN: 占卜官在划定的圣域内观察。

items.example: The temple stood above the harbour.

items.meaning: the flat side of the forehead
items.example: A pulse beat at his temple.
items.exampleCN: 他的太阳穴处有脉搏跳动。

items.example: The headache sat behind both temples.
items.exampleCN: 头痛压在两侧太阳穴后面。

items.example: The verb began as watching the sky.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词最初指观察天空。
