items.example: The reading room has a temple-like calm.
items.exampleCN: 这间阅览室有一种神庙般的宁静。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 时间；复数指头部太阳穴

definition_zh: 优美的；优雅的；得体的
definition_en: moving or shaped with smooth beauty, or behaving in a polite and dignified way
core_image: 天鹅在水面上滑行，长颈弯成一道平滑的弧线
scene: 天鹅在水面上划出优美的弧线。 The swan made a graceful curve on the water.
sceneCN: 这里 graceful 是「优美的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：天鹅在水面上划出优美的弧线。

senses.title: Beautiful in movement
senses.definition: moving in a smooth and attractive way
senses.definitionCN: 以平滑而悦目的方式移动
senses.example: The swan made a graceful curve on the water.
senses.exampleCN: 天鹅在水面上划出优美的弧线。
senses.why: This is the central sense of pleasing motion.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示动作悦目的核心含义。

senses.title: Dignified in conduct
senses.definition: behaving in a polite and dignified way, especially in difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在困境中举止礼貌而有尊严
senses.example: She made a graceful exit from the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她体面地退出了会议。
senses.why: The beauty of movement became a beauty of manners.
senses.whyCN: 动作之美延伸为举止之美。

senses.title: Smooth in line
senses.definition: having a smooth and pleasing shape or line
senses.definitionCN: 具有平滑悦目的形状或线条
senses.example: The bridge has a graceful line.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的线条很流畅。
senses.why: Shape borrowed the same word as movement.
senses.whyCN: 形状借用了与动作相同的词。

intro.en: Graceful is grace with the Old English ending -ful, full of grace.
intro.cn: graceful 是 grace 加古英语词尾 -ful，意为充满优雅。

items.en: Gratia meant favour and pleasing quality.
items.cn: gratia 意为恩惠与令人愉快的品质。

items.en: Grace named a pleasing manner.
items.cn: grace 指讨人喜欢的举止。

items.en: Grace entered English as elegance and favour.
items.cn: grace 以优雅和恩惠之义进入英语。

items.en: Graceful was formed to mean full of grace.
items.cn: graceful 被构造成「充满优雅」之意。

items.en: It spread from bodies to lines and manners.
items.cn: 它从身体扩展到线条和举止。

note.en: Graceful is compared with look-alike words and words for elegance.
note.cn: 把 graceful 与形近词以及表示优雅的词作比较。

without grace

normalIntro.en: Graceful is what grace looks like when it moves.
normalIntro.cn: graceful 是优雅动起来的样子。

normal.en: The swan made a graceful curve on the water.
normal.cn: 天鹅在水面上划出优美的弧线。

normal.en: She made a graceful exit from the meeting.
normal.cn: 她体面地退出了会议。

normal.en: The bridge has a graceful line.
normal.cn: 这座桥的线条很流畅。

normal.en: The dancer's movements were graceful.
normal.cn: 舞者的动作优美。

normal.en: He offered a graceful apology.
normal.cn: 他作出了得体的道歉。

abstract.en: Graceful is effort that has learned to hide.
abstract.cn: 优美，是学会了隐藏的用力。

abstract.en: A graceful exit says more than a loud entrance.
abstract.cn: 体面的退场胜过喧闹的登场。

abstract.en: Line and limb obey the same quiet law.
abstract.cn: 线条与肢体遵循同一条安静的法则。

examples.en: The swan made a graceful curve on the water.
examples.cn: 天鹅在水面上划出优美的弧线。

dict_mnemonic.text: graceful 由 grace（优雅）加形容词词尾 -ful 构成，表示「优美的、得体的」；gracefully 是「优雅地」，gracefulness 是「优雅」，注意与 grateful（感激的）区分。

root: 由 grace（源自拉丁语 gratia，恩惠、优雅）加古英语形容词词尾 -ful 构成，本义为充满优雅的，引申为动作优美、举止得体、线条流畅。

sensesIntro.en: Graceful means beautiful in movement, dignified in conduct, or smooth in shape.
sensesIntro.cn: graceful 指动作优美、举止得体，或形状线条流畅。

core.en: Ease made visible.
core.cn: 变得可见的从容。

branches.en: A swan draws a curve across still water.
branches.cn: 天鹅在静水上画出一道弧线。

branches.en: A person leaves a meeting with dignity.
branches.cn: 一个人带着尊严离开会议。

branches.en: A bridge arcs without a single sharp turn.
branches.cn: 一座桥弯成弧线，没有一处尖角。

branches.en: Movement and line share the same smooth law.
branches.cn: 动作与线条共享同一条平滑法则。

branches.en: Beauty of body and beauty of manner meet in one word.
branches.cn: 身体之美与举止之美在一个词里相遇。

intro.en: Graceful forms adverbs and nouns of elegance.
intro.cn: graceful 构成表示优雅的副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is gratia, favour, from gratus, pleasing.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 gratia（恩惠），源于 gratus（令人愉快的）。

items.example: The swan made a graceful curve on the water.
items.exampleCN: 天鹅在水面上划出优美的弧线。

items.example: She stepped gracefully onto the stage.

items.exampleCN: 她跳舞时带着一种自然的优雅。

items.example: It was a graceless way to refuse.
items.exampleCN: 那是一种不得体的拒绝方式。

items.example: Our host was gracious and warm.
He brought disgrace on his family.

definition_zh: 禁止；不准；使不可能
definition_en: to order that something must not be done, or to make something impossible
core_image: 一只手掌竖在门前，掌心朝外，示意不许进入
scene: 医院里禁止吸烟。 Smoking is forbidden in the hospital.
sceneCN: 这里 forbid 是「禁止」（第 1 个义项）；句意：医院里禁止吸烟。

senses.title: Order against
senses.definition: to order that something must not be done
senses.definitionCN: 命令某事不得做
senses.example: Smoking is forbidden in the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 医院里禁止吸烟。
senses.why: This is the main modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的现代义项。

senses.title: Refuse permission
senses.definition: to refuse to allow someone to do something
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝允许某人做某事
senses.example: Her parents forbade her to go alone.
senses.exampleCN: 她父母不准她独自去。
senses.why: The order is aimed at a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个命令指向具体的人。

senses.title: Make impossible
senses.definition: to make something impossible
senses.definitionCN: 使某事不可能发生
senses.example: The storm forbade any attempt to sail.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨使任何出航尝试都不可能。
senses.why: A strong barrier forbids by circumstance.
senses.whyCN: 强大的阻碍以环境条件禁止。

intro.en: Forbid is an old compound of for- and bid, to command.
intro.cn: forbid 是 for- 与 bid（命令）构成的古老复合词。

items.en: Forbeodan meant to command against.
items.cn: forbeodan 意为下令禁止。

items.en: Forbede kept the sense of refusing permission.
items.cn: forbede 保留了不准许的含义。

items.en: Forbid extended to things made impossible.
items.cn: forbid 扩展到使不可能的事情。

items.en: Forbidden became common in rules and signs.
items.cn: forbidden 在规则与标牌中变得常见。

items.en: God forbid became a fixed expression.
items.cn: God forbid 成为固定表达。

note.en: Forbid is compared with similar-looking words and with words for banning.
note.cn: 把 forbid 与形近词以及表示禁止的词作比较。

entries.definition: to fail to remember
to stop being angry with someone
to hold back from doing something
to officially forbid something
to forbid by law or rule
to stop something from happening

normalIntro.en: To forbid is to put a firm hand in front of an action.
normalIntro.cn: forbid 就是在某个动作前竖起一只坚决的手。

normal.en: The school forbids mobile phones.
normal.cn: 学校禁止使用手机。

normal.en: Her father forbade her to leave.
normal.cn: 她父亲不准她离开。

normal.en: Smoking is forbidden here.
normal.cn: 这里禁止吸烟。

normal.en: The weather forbade an early start.
normal.cn: 天气使提早出发变得不可能。

normal.en: Forbidden fruit always looks sweet.
normal.cn: 禁果总是显得甜美。

abstract.en: A ban is a wall made of words.
abstract.cn: 禁令是用语言筑起的墙。

abstract.en: Forbidding something often makes it more tempting.
abstract.cn: 禁止某物常让它更诱人。

abstract.en: Some limits are set by weather, not by people.
abstract.cn: 有些限制由天气而非人设定。

examples.en: Smoking is forbidden in the hospital.
examples.cn: 医院里禁止吸烟。

examples.en: Her parents forbade her to go alone.
examples.cn: 她父母不准她独自去。

examples.en: The storm forbade any attempt to sail.
examples.cn: 暴风雨使任何出航尝试都不可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: forbid 由 for-（否定、禁止）加 bid（命令）组成：下命令说「不许」。

root: 源自古英语 forbeodan（下令禁止），核心义「以命令挡住某事」。

sensesIntro.en: Forbid means to order against, refuse permission, or make impossible.
sensesIntro.cn: forbid 意为禁止、不准或使不可能。

core.en: A command that stops an action before it starts.
core.cn: 在行动开始前拦住它的命令。

branches.en: A rule says no smoking.
branches.cn: 规定说禁止吸烟。

branches.en: A parent refuses permission.
branches.cn: 父母不准许。

branches.en: A storm blocks the voyage.
branches.cn: 暴风雨挡住航行。

branches.en: Rules and parents both say no.
branches.cn: 规则与父母都在说不行。

branches.en: Circumstances can forbid without speaking.
branches.cn: 环境不用开口也能禁止。

intro.en: Forbid forms a family of prohibition words.
intro.cn: forbid 形成一个表示禁止的词族。

latinIntro.en: Forbid has no Latin ancestor; Latin prohibere, to forbid, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: forbid 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 prohibere（禁止）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The law forbids the sale of fireworks.

items.exampleCN: 那处悬崖看上去令人生畏。
这条路没有被禁止通行。

definition_zh: 卫生间；厕所；马桶；盥洗间
definition_en: a room with a toilet, the toilet itself, or in older use a place for washing
core_image: 车站尽头一扇小门，门牌上画着一滴水
scene: 火车快到站时，走廊尽头的小门前已经排起了队。 He asked the conductor where the lavatory was.
sceneCN: 这里是「卫生间、厕所」（第 1 个义项：带马桶的房间）；句意为他问乘务员洗手间在哪里。可辨识画面：车厢走廊、门前排队的人、门上的小标志。

pos.zh: 卫生间；厕所；马桶；盥洗间

derivatives.zh: 由 lavatory 加 -ial 构成，义为「厕所的」；也指「粗俗下流的」
由拉丁词干 lav-（洗）加 -ation 构成，义为「洗涤」
来自拉丁语 lavabo（我要洗手），义为「洗手盆；洗手礼」

senses.title: A room with a toilet
senses.definition: a room, especially a public one, with a toilet and usually a washbasin
senses.definitionCN: 设有马桶、通常也有洗手盆的房间，尤指公共的
senses.example: The lavatory is at the end of the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 洗手间在走廊尽头。
senses.why: Latin lavare meant to wash, and a room named after washing kept that name even when the toilet became its main purpose.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 lavare 意为洗，这个以「洗」命名的房间即使马桶成了主要用途，也沿用旧名。

senses.title: The toilet itself
senses.definition: the bowl and seat used as a toilet
senses.definitionCN: 用作马桶的便盆与座圈
senses.example: The lavatory would not flush.
senses.exampleCN: 马桶冲不下去了。
senses.why: Since people name a room by the fixture they go there for, the word for the room shifted onto the bowl inside it.
senses.whyCN: 既然人们用房间里的主要设施来指这个房间，房间的名字就落到了里面的便器上。

senses.title: A place for washing, the older sense
senses.definition: a room or basin used for washing, the original meaning of the word
senses.definitionCN: 用于洗浴或洗手的房间、盆具，是这个词较早的含义
senses.example: The older house had a lavatory off the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 那栋老房子的门厅旁有一间盥洗室。
senses.why: The word began as a washing place, and this sense survives in older buildings and in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指洗浴之处，这层意思在老式建筑与正式文字里仍然保留。

intro.en: A Latin verb of washing and a Latin place suffix made a word for a washing place, which English later moved to the toilet.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「洗」的动词与一个拉丁语地点后缀造出了「洗浴之处」，英语后来把它移到了厕所上。

items.en: Lavare meant to wash, and it is the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: lavare 意为洗，是这一族词背后的动词。

items.en: Lavatorium named a place for washing, built from the verb and a place suffix.
items.cn: lavatorium 指洗浴之处，由动词加地点后缀构成。

items.en: The word entered church Latin for the basin used in washing rites.
items.cn: 这个词进入教会拉丁语，指行洗礼仪式的盆。

items.en: English lavatory first meant a washing place or a basin, not a toilet.
items.cn: 英语 lavatory 最初指洗浴处或盆具，并非厕所。

items.en: Modern English shifted the word to the room with a toilet, especially in British use.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词转到带马桶的房间，尤见于英式用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the lav- stem or merely the shape; the near-meaning group collects the many polite words for a toilet.
note.cn: 形近组收共用 lav- 词干或只是形状相近的词；近义组收各种对厕所的礼貌说法。

entries.definition: A room for scientific work, close in shape but not in history.
entries.definitionCN: 进行科学工作的房间；形状相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Giving or spending very generously.
entries.definitionCN: 非常大方地给予或花费。

entries.definition: Medical washing out of a body cavity or organ.
entries.definitionCN: 医学上对体腔或器官的冲洗。

entries.definition: Molten rock pouring from a volcano.
The fixture itself, or the room containing it.
entries.definitionCN: 马桶本身，或装有马桶的房间。

entries.definition: A room for washing, used politely for a toilet in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 洗澡的房间；美式英语中委婉地指厕所。

entries.definition: A room with washing and toilet facilities.
entries.definitionCN: 设有盥洗与如厕设施的房间。

entries.definition: A public toilet, the usual polite word in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 公共厕所，美式英语常用的委婉说法。

normalIntro.en: A verb of washing and a suffix for places explain why this word still sounds like a bathroom in older writing.
normalIntro.cn: 一个「洗」的动词与一个表示地点的后缀，解释了为什么这个词在旧文字里仍像一间盥洗室。

normal.en: Lavare is Latin for to wash, so lavatory begins as a washing place.
normal.cn: lavare 是拉丁语的「洗」，所以 lavatory 原指洗的地方。

normal.en: The ending -torium marks a place, the same shape seen in other Latin place names.
normal.cn: 词尾 -torium 标记地点，在其他拉丁地点名词里也能见到同一形状。

normal.en: Lavatory and lavation share the lav- stem, which is the washing part.
normal.cn: lavatory 与 lavation 共用 lav- 词干，就是「洗」的部分。

normal.en: British English keeps lavatory for a public toilet, while American English prefers restroom.
normal.cn: 英式英语用 lavatory 指公共厕所，美式英语更常用 restroom。

normal.en: Lavatory seat is the part you sit on, a phrase that shows the fixture sense.
normal.cn: lavatory seat 指坐上去的那部分，这个搭配体现了「便器」义。

abstract.en: A room named for washing kept its name when its job changed, a small record of how plumbing moved.
abstract.cn: 一个以「洗」命名的房间在用途改变后仍沿用旧名，这是管道设施变迁的小记录。

abstract.en: The word's politeness comes from distance: it mentions washing instead of what happens there.
abstract.cn: 这个词的委婉来自距离：它提的是洗手，而不是那里真正发生的事。

abstract.en: A Latin place suffix turns an action into a room, so a verb of washing becomes a door you can open.
abstract.cn: 拉丁语的地点后缀把动作变成房间，于是「洗」这个动词成了一扇可以推开的门。

examples.en: The lavatory is at the end of the corridor.
examples.cn: 洗手间在走廊尽头。

examples.en: He asked the conductor where the lavatory was.
examples.cn: 他问乘务员洗手间在哪里。

examples.en: The lavatory would not flush.
examples.cn: 马桶冲不下去了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉水」——上完厕所要拉一下水冲干净；记住 lavatory 是厕所。

root: 拉丁语 lavare（洗）加地点后缀 -torium 构成 lavatorium（洗浴之处），后经教会拉丁语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place for washing; the senses then move to the room with a toilet, the fixture inside it, and the older washing sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是洗浴之处；义项由此转到带马桶的房间、房内的便器，以及较早的洗涤义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small door at the end of a train corridor with a drop of water on its sign.
core.cn: 核心意象：车厢走廊尽头一扇小门，门牌上画着一滴水。

branches.en: a queue outside a door at the end of a carriage
branches.cn: 车厢尽头门前排队的人

branches.en: a handle pulled to flush a bowl
branches.cn: 拉动冲水的把手

branches.en: a basin standing in an old stone washroom
branches.cn: 旧石头盥洗室里的一只盆

branches.en: a sign showing a drop of water on a door
branches.cn: 门上画着一滴水的标志

branches.en: a row of washing bowls in a church
branches.cn: 教堂里一排用于洗礼仪式的盆

intro.en: A Latin verb of washing, a Latin place suffix and one English adjective ending build this word.
intro.cn: 一个表示洗的拉丁动词、一个拉丁地点后缀与一个英语形容词词尾构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: room for washing, then a toilet
I shall wash, a washing basin

definition_zh: 传送；发射；传输；传播（疾病、情感）
definition_en: to send out signals, to pass something such as a disease or a feeling to others, or to send power through a wire
core_image: 山顶天线在雨里一闪一闪地把声音发向云层
scene: 雨夜的广播站，天线塔顶端的红灯一亮一暗。 The station transmits news to the whole coast every hour.
sceneCN: 这里 transmit 是「发射；传送」（第 1 个义项：把信号发出去）；句意为这家电台每小时向整个海岸发送一次新闻。雨里一闪一闪的天线，就是这个词的形象。

derivatives.zh: 由 transmit 加 -ssion 构成，义为「传送；传输」
由 transmit 加 -er 构成，义为「发射机；传送者」
由 transmit 加 -able 构成，义为「可传送的；可传播的」

senses.title: Sending a signal out
senses.definition: to send out an electronic signal such as radio waves or a picture
senses.definitionCN: 发出无线电波、图像等电子信号
senses.example: The station transmits news to the whole coast every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这家电台每小时向整个海岸发送一次新闻。
senses.why: Latin mittere means to send, and trans adds the direction, so the verb is simply to send across.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mittere 意为送，trans 补上方向，于是这个动词就是「送过去」。

senses.title: Passing on illness
senses.definition: to pass an infection or a parasite from one living thing to another
senses.definitionCN: 把感染或寄生虫从一种生物传给另一种
senses.example: Mosquitoes can transmit several dangerous fevers.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子能传播好几种危险的发热病。
senses.why: When a mosquito carries a germ to a new body, it does exactly what a wire does with a signal.
senses.whyCN: 当蚊子把病菌带到新的身体里，它做的事和导线对待信号完全一样。

senses.title: Carrying heat or force
senses.definition: to allow heat, sound, or force to pass through a material
senses.definitionCN: 让热、声或力通过某种材料传过
senses.example: Metal transmits heat faster than wood.
senses.exampleCN: 金属导热比木头快。
senses.why: Physics borrowed the everyday verb because energy also crosses from one place to another.
senses.whyCN: 物理学借用了这个日常动词，因为能量也同样从一处走到另一处。

senses.title: Passing on a feeling
senses.definition: to make other people feel the emotion you feel
senses.definitionCN: 让别人感受到你所感受的情绪
senses.example: Her calm voice transmitted confidence to the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她平静的声音把信心传给了整支队伍。
senses.why: A feeling can travel from one mind to another, so the word reaches beyond wires and bodies.
senses.whyCN: 情绪能从一个心灵传到另一个心灵，于是这个词越过了导线与身体。

intro.en: Transmit is the Latin verb transmittere, to send across, taken into English with its two parts still visible.
intro.cn: transmit 是拉丁语动词 transmittere（送过去）原样进入英语，两部分仍然清晰可见。

items.en: Mittere, to send, is one of the busiest verbs of Latin motion.
items.cn: mittere（送）是拉丁语中最常用的运动动词之一。

items.en: Transmittere meant to send a thing over or through, from a hand to a place.
items.cn: transmittere 意为把东西送过或送穿，从一只手到一处地方。

items.en: French kept transmettre, used for handing on property as well as objects.
items.cn: 法语保留 transmettre，既用于递交物品也用于转让财产。

items.en: English took transmit first for the passing on of disease and of rights.
items.cn: 英语最初用 transmit 表示疾病与权利的传递。

items.en: Telegraph and radio gave the verb its modern electronic sense.
items.cn: 电报与无线电赋予这个动词现代的电子含义。

note.en: The first group shows forms of the same verb, the second shows other verbs of sending and spreading.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词的各种形式，第二组是其他表示发送与扩散的动词。

entries.definition: The act of sending or passing on.
A device that sends out signals.
Sent out or passed on in the past.
To send out a programme to many listeners.
To carry or make a feeling understood.
To move over a wider area.

normalIntro.en: Transmit keeps the trans of crossing and the mit of sending, and doubles its t before endings.
normalIntro.cn: transmit 保留 trans（跨越）与 mit（送），在加词尾前要把 t 双写。

normal.en: Mit is the same root as in submit and admit.
normal.cn: mit 与 submit、admit 里的词根相同。

normal.en: The past tense doubles the last letter: transmitted.
normal.cn: 过去式双写末字母：transmitted。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable: transMIT.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：transMIT。

normal.en: A transmitter does the sending, a transmission is the sending itself.
normal.cn: transmitter 执行发送，transmission 是发送这件事。

normal.en: Radio waves transmit without any wire at all.
normal.cn: 无线电波根本不需要导线就能传送。

abstract.en: A red light blinking on a tower at night.
abstract.cn: 夜里塔上闪烁的一点红光。

abstract.en: A word leaving one mouth and arriving in many ears.
abstract.cn: 一句话离开一张嘴，落进许多只耳朵。

abstract.en: Heat moving quietly along a metal spoon.
abstract.cn: 热安静地沿着金属勺子移动。

examples.en: The tower transmits the signal to ships far out at sea.
examples.cn: 这座塔把信号传送给远在海上的船只。

examples.en: Some insects transmit disease when they bite.
examples.cn: 有些昆虫叮咬时会传播疾病。

examples.en: Copper transmits electricity better than iron.
examples.cn: 铜导电比铁好。

dict_mnemonic.text: trans（越过）＋ mit（送）——把信号送越距离，就是发射传送。

root: 拉丁语 transmittere，trans（越过）＋ mittere（送），本义「送过去」；同族词有 transmission、transmitter、transmittable。

sensesIntro.en: The electronic signal comes first, then disease, then heat and force, then feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是电子信号，再是疾病，然后是热与力，最后是情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tower light blinking in rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨里闪烁的塔灯。

branches.en: The signal branch: waves leaving the antenna.
branches.cn: 信号分支：离开天线的波。

branches.en: The illness branch: germs carried by a bite.
branches.cn: 疾病分支：被叮咬带走的病菌。

branches.en: The material branch: heat allowed to pass through.
branches.cn: 材料分支：允许热穿过的物体。

branches.en: The feeling branch: calm travelling to others.
branches.cn: 情感分支：平静传给他人。

branches.en: The unseen branch: nothing visible ever moves.
branches.cn: 无形分支：看不见任何东西真正移动。

intro.en: Transmit is trans plus the Latin root mit, and it gains -er, -able and -ssion in its family.
intro.cn: transmit 是 trans 加拉丁词根 mit，词族中再加 -er、-able 与 -ssion。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 mittere（送）出现在许多英语动词中，下面列出其中四条。

definition_zh: 平静地；镇定地
definition_en: in a quiet and steady way
core_image: 语气平稳、手势缓慢的样子
scene: 火警灯闪起来，人群开始骚动。 She calmly told everyone to walk outside.

derivatives.zh: 平静的，calmly 的形容词基础

senses.title: In a steady, unshaken way

definition_zh: 纯粹的；陡峭的；极薄的；完全地
definition_en: complete and nothing else, very steep, very thin and transparent, or completely
core_image: 一面几乎垂直的岩壁，从水面直插天空
scene: 悬崖从海面陡然升起。 The cliff rises sheer from the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 sheer 是「陡峭的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：悬崖从海面陡然升起。

senses.title: Complete
senses.definition: used to emphasize that something is nothing but what is stated
senses.definitionCN: 强调某事物完全是所说的那样
senses.example: It was sheer luck that we met.
senses.exampleCN: 我们相遇纯属运气。
senses.why: This is the most common modern use.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的用法。

senses.title: Very steep
senses.definition: rising almost straight up
senses.definitionCN: 几乎垂直升起的
senses.example: The cliff rises sheer from the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 悬崖从海面陡然升起。
senses.why: A sheer face has no slope to hold on to.
senses.whyCN: 陡壁没有任何可攀附的斜坡。

senses.title: Very thin
senses.definition: thin, light, and almost transparent

senses.why: Thin cloth lets light through like clear air.
senses.whyCN: 薄布像清澈空气一样透光。

senses.title: Completely
senses.definition: used as an adverb meaning completely
senses.definitionCN: 作副词表示完全地
senses.example: The door was sheer impossible to open.
senses.exampleCN: 那扇门根本打不开。
senses.why: Pure emphasis turns the adjective into an adverb.
senses.whyCN: 纯粹的强调使形容词转为副词。

intro.en: Sheer joins an Old English word for bright and clear with a Norse word for steep.

definition_zh: 收养的；（移居后）归属的
definition_en: related by adoption rather than by birth, or describing a country or place someone has chosen to live in
core_image: 相册里一张合影，孩子坐在两位大人中间，笑得很自然
scene: 他在异国住了三十年，早把那里当成自己的家。 He calls Canada his adoptive country.
sceneCN: 这里的 adoptive 是「移居后归属的」（第 2 个义项：自己选择并长期生活的）；句意是他把加拿大称作自己的归化国。

pos.zh: 形容词：收养的；移居后归属的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词词干还原为动词，义为「收养；采用」

senses.title: Related through adoption
senses.definition: describing a parent, child or family joined by adoption rather than by birth
senses.definitionCN: 指通过收养而非血缘建立关系的父母、子女或家庭
senses.example: His adoptive parents moved to Spain when he was six.
senses.exampleCN: 他六岁时，养父母搬到了西班牙。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the -ive ending of a describing word and marks the side that does the adopting, as opposed to the child, who is adopted.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词保留 -ive 词尾，标记「实施收养」的那一方，与「被收养」的孩子相对。

senses.title: Chosen as one's country or home
senses.definition: describing a place that someone has chosen to live in and come to regard as home
senses.definitionCN: 指某人选择定居并认作故乡的地方
senses.example: The writer made Paris his adoptive home.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家把巴黎当作自己的第二故乡。
senses.why: A country can be chosen the way a child is: it is taken into one's life and called one's own.
senses.whyCN: 国家也可以像孩子一样被「选择」：它被接进一个人的生活，并被称为自己的。

intro.en: An adjective of choosing, applied to people and to places.
intro.cn: 一个表示「选择」的形容词，用在人身上，也用在地方上。

items.en: optare meant to choose or wish.
items.cn: optare 意为选择、希望。

items.en: adoptare meant to take as one's own by choice.
items.cn: adoptare 意为「选来作为自己的」。

items.cn: adoptivus 是表示「属于收养的」的形容词。

items.en: English adopted the adjective in the seventeenth century, chiefly for parents and children.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入这个形容词，主要用于父母与子女。

items.en: Travel and migration extended it to countries and cities that people choose as home.
items.cn: 旅行与移民把它扩展到人们选择定居的国家与城市。

note.en: The first group shares the choosing root; the second contrasts chosen and birth relationships.
note.cn: 第一组共享「选择」词根；第二组对照「选择」与「血缘」两类关系。

intro.en: Sunshine builds sunshiny and pairs with sunshade.
intro.cn: sunshine 可构成 sunshiny，并与 sunshade 同族。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Germanic: sunne and scinan.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都属日耳曼语：sunne 与 scinan。

items.exampleCN: 那是一个阳光明媚的早晨。
阳光照亮的路上空无一人。

latinEntries.example: Sunne is the first part of sunshine.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sunne 是 sunshine 的第一部分来源。

definition_zh: 不成功的；失败的；落空的
definition_en: not achieving the result that was intended
core_image: 一扇门推了三次都没开
scene: 年轻人提前半年准备面试，结果名单公布时还是没能进去。 He was unsuccessful in his attempt to join the team.
sceneCN: 这里 unsuccessful 是「不成功的」（第 1 个义项：没能达到目的）；句意为他那次想进这支队伍的尝试没有成功。推了三次都没开的门，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不成功地；失败地」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「成功的」
同源动词，义为「成功；接替」

senses.title: Not reaching the goal
senses.definition: not achieving the aim one set out to reach
senses.definitionCN: 没有达到原先设定的目标
senses.example: The rescue attempt was unsuccessful, and the boat drifted on.
senses.exampleCN: 救援的尝试没有成功，船继续漂了下去。
senses.why: The word is the negative of successful, whose base success came to mean a good outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 successful 的反面，而 success 的本义已经变成「好的结果」。

senses.title: A request or application that is turned down
senses.definition: used of a formal request or application that is refused
senses.definitionCN: 形容正式申请或请求被拒绝
senses.example: His application for the scholarship was unsuccessful.
senses.exampleCN: 他的奖学金申请没有通过。
senses.why: An application is a formal attempt, and when it is refused the door simply does not open.
senses.whyCN: 申请是一种正式的尝试，被拒时那扇门就是没有开。

senses.title: Effort that brings no result
senses.definition: used of attempts that use effort but bring nothing
senses.definitionCN: 形容花了力气却毫无收获
senses.example: Their attempts to save the old tree were unsuccessful.
senses.exampleCN: 他们救那棵老树的努力白费了。
senses.why: The core image is effort pushing against a closed door, so the word naturally names work that yields nothing.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是力气顶在一扇不开的门上，因此这个词自然用来形容花了力气却无所得。

senses.title: A person who has not yet succeeded in a field
senses.definition: used of a person who has not yet achieved recognition in a field
senses.definitionCN: 形容在某个领域尚未取得成就的人
senses.example: As an unsuccessful writer he taught school to pay the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 作为尚未成名的作家，他靠教书付房租。
senses.why: When the negative applies to a person, the idea shifts from the attempt to the standing that the attempt never brought.
senses.whyCN: 当否定落在人身上，这层意思就从「那次尝试」转到「尝试始终没带来的地位」。

senses.title: A search or test that finds nothing
senses.definition: used of a search, test, or trial that turns up no answer
senses.definitionCN: 形容查找、试验或审讯毫无答案
senses.example: An unsuccessful search for the key went on until dark.
senses.exampleCN: 找钥匙一直毫无结果，直到天黑。
senses.why: A search is an attempt aimed at a find, so a search that finds nothing is the same missed door.
senses.whyCN: 搜寻本就是奔着找到东西去的一次尝试，因此一无所获的搜寻还是那扇没开的门。

intro.en: A negative prefix over an adjective from Latin successus, a going up or a good outcome.
intro.cn: 否定前缀压在由拉丁语 successus（上升、好结果）来的形容词上。

items.en: The native prefix un- reverses the meaning of adjectives of any origin.
items.cn: 本土前缀 un- 可反转任何来源形容词的词义。

items.en: Succedere meant to come next or to go up from below.
items.cn: succedere 意为「随后而来」或「从下面升上去」。

items.en: The noun succès named the result of an affair, good or bad.
items.cn: 法语名词 succès 指一件事的结局，好坏皆可。

items.en: Success enters English in the sixteenth century and settles on the good outcome.
items.cn: success 于十六世纪进入英语，后来固定指「好的结果」。

items.en: Successful and then unsuccessful follow, first of events and later of people.
items.cn: 随后出现 successful 与 unsuccessful，先用于事件，后用于人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the success family, and the near-meaning group collects words of failure and frustration.
note.cn: 形近组沿 success 词族展开，近义组汇集表示失败与落空的词。

entries.definition: reaching the aim
without success
the achievement of an aim
to do what was intended
a series of things one after another
having not succeeded
producing no result
producing no effect
producing the intended result

normalIntro.en: The word is the negative of one of the most transparent adjectives in English.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是英语里最透明的形容词之一的否定形式。

normal.en: Un- plus successful: the aim was set and not reached.
normal.cn: un- 加 successful：目标设在前面却没走到。

normal.en: Be unsuccessful in doing something is the fixed frame.
normal.cn: be unsuccessful in doing 是固定框架。

normal.en: An unsuccessful attempt and an unsuccessful application are the two common partners.
normal.cn: an unsuccessful attempt 与 an unsuccessful application 是两个常见搭配。

normal.en: Success, succeed, and succession all come from Latin succedere.
normal.cn: success、succeed、succession 都来自拉丁语 succedere。

normal.en: Weather reports say an overnight search proved unsuccessful.
normal.cn: 天气新闻里常说一夜的搜寻未能成功。

abstract.en: See a door that does not open after three pushes.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇推了三次都没开的门。

abstract.en: Watch a fishing boat come back with an empty net.
abstract.cn: 看一艘渔船带着空网回来。

abstract.en: Feel the small hesitation before you read a list of names.
abstract.cn: 体会在读名单之前的那一下迟疑。

examples.en: The first attempt to repair the bridge was unsuccessful.
examples.cn: 第一次修桥的尝试没有成功。

examples.en: She was unsuccessful in her application for a transfer.
examples.cn: 她的调动申请没有通过。

examples.en: Their search for the missing dog proved unsuccessful for two days.
examples.cn: 他们找那只走失的狗，两天都没有结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺塞成功」——怎么塞都塞不进去，成功俩字一直没能塞进手里。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ successful（成功的），successful 来自名词 success，success 源自拉丁语 successus / succedere（随之而来、由下升起）

sensesIntro.en: One idea, the aim was missed, covers attempts, applications, wasted effort, careers, and fruitless searches.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个意思「目标没落到手」，覆盖尝试、申请、白费力气、事业与毫无结果的查找。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door that does not give way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇怎么推也不让开的门。

branches.en: The plain branch: the goal simply was not reached.
branches.cn: 朴素分支：目标就是没达到。

branches.en: The formal branch: an application comes back refused.
branches.cn: 正式分支：申请被退回来。

branches.en: The waste branch: effort that leaves nothing behind.
branches.cn: 落空分支：力气花完什么也没留下。

branches.en: The career branch: someone still waiting to be recognised.
branches.cn: 事业分支：仍在等被看见的人。

branches.en: The search branch: a hunt that turns up nothing.
branches.cn: 查访分支：一无所获的搜寻。

intro.en: A native negative prefix sits over a Latin-derived adjective whose own suffix is very common.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在拉丁来源的形容词上，其自身的后缀非常常见。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is succedere, made of sub- under and cedere to go.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁来源是 succedere，由 sub-（在下）与 cedere（走）组成。

items.example: Succedere begins with sub- before c moved.
items.exampleCN: succedere 在 c 前用了 sub- 的变体。
cedere 是 proceed 与 concede 的词根。

items.meaning: to come after or do well

latinEntries.meaning: to come after, to go up

definition_zh: 随意的；非正式的；漫不经心的；临时的
definition_en: relaxed and informal in manner or dress, not showing much care, or happening by chance and without a plan
core_image: 没有事先安排、随手就来的样子
scene: 公司周五允许员工不穿西装。 On Fridays the office has a casual dress code.
sceneCN: 这里 casual 指「随意的」（第 1 个义项：不正式、轻松的穿着方式）；句意是每逢周五，办公室执行休闲着装规定。

pos.zh: 随意的；非正式的；漫不经心的；临时的

senses.title: Relaxed and informal
senses.definition: relaxed in style, not formal or planned, especially of clothes or gatherings
senses.definitionCN: 风格轻松，不正式或没有安排，尤指衣着或聚会
senses.example: He wore casual clothes to the dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着休闲服去参加晚宴。
senses.why: What happens by chance has no ceremony, so dress without ceremony becomes casual dress.
senses.whyCN: 偶然发生的事没有仪式感，于是不带仪式感的穿着就成了 casual 的穿着。

senses.title: Showing little care
senses.definition: done without attention or serious thought, sometimes causing harm
senses.definitionCN: 做事不加注意或不认真思考，有时造成损害
senses.example: A casual remark hurt her feelings.
senses.exampleCN: 一句随口的话伤了她的心。
senses.why: An unplanned act is also an unconsidered one, so the chance sense shades into carelessness.
senses.whyCN: 没有计划的行为也往往没有经过思考，于是偶然义渐渐带上马虎义。

senses.title: Temporary or occasional
senses.definition: employed for a short time or happening at irregular intervals
senses.definitionCN: 短期受雇的，或间隔不固定地发生的
senses.example: The hotel hires casual staff in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店夏天雇临时工。
senses.why: Work that comes by chance rather than by contract is casual work, done by casual workers.
senses.whyCN: 靠机会而非合同来的工作就是临时工作，由临时工来做。

intro.en: Casual goes back to the Latin word for a fall or event, so its first meaning is simply what happens by chance.
intro.cn: casual 可追到拉丁语中表示落下或事件的词，所以它最初的意思就是偶然发生的。

items.en: Casus meant a fall or an event, from cadere, to fall.
items.cn: 拉丁语 casus 意为落下或事件，源自动词 cadere（落下）。

items.en: Casualis described whatever happened by chance rather than by design.
items.cn: casualis 形容偶然发生、并非有意安排的事。

items.en: Casuel carried the chance sense into medieval French and then into English.
items.cn: 古法语 casuel 把偶然义带入中古法语，再进入英语。

items.en: English casual first means happening by chance, without plan or regularity.
items.cn: 英语 casual 最初指偶然发生、没有计划或规律。

items.en: The word extends to informal dress, relaxed manners and short-term work.
items.cn: 此后词义扩展到休闲衣着、随便的举止和短期工作。

items.en: Casual Friday and casual wear now fix the relaxed sense in everyday use.
items.cn: casual Friday 与 casual wear 让轻松义在日常用语中固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the chance root through its adverbs and nouns, while the meaning group offers nearby adjectives.
note.cn: 形近组沿偶然这一词根经副词与名词展开，近义组给出相近的形容词。

entries.definition: in a relaxed or careless way
the quality of being informal
a person killed or injured in an accident or war
entries.definitionCN: 在事故或战争中死伤的人

entries.definition: relaxed and without strict rules
calm and not worried
happening by chance, not on purpose

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie casual to the event root, to the -ly adverb and to the everyday dress phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 casual 与事件词根、-ly 副词和日常着装搭配连起来。

normal.en: Casual shares its root with case: both come from casus, an event that falls out.
normal.cn: casual 与 case 同根，都来自 casus，即落下来的事件。

normal.en: Casualty began as a chance event and now means a person hurt by one.
normal.cn: casualty 最初指偶然事件，现在指在事件中受伤的人。

normal.en: Casual clothes and casual Friday keep the informal sense visible every week.
normal.cn: casual clothes 和 casual Friday 每周都在提醒非正式这一含义。

normal.en: The -ly adverb casually simply adds the manner sense to the adjective.
normal.cn: 副词 casually 只是在形容词上加了方式义。

normal.en: More casual and most casual take a helper word because the adjective is long.
normal.cn: 因为词形较长，比较级和最高级用 more 与 most 来构成。

abstract.en: Picture a man in sandals at a formal dinner, completely at ease.
abstract.cn: 想象一位穿凉鞋出席正式晚宴却毫不拘束的男子。

abstract.en: Picture a remark tossed out without thinking, then landing hard.
abstract.cn: 想象一句没经思考就抛出的话，落地却很重。

abstract.en: Picture a worker hired for one busy weekend and paid by the day.
abstract.cn: 想象一个只在忙碌周末受雇、按天结钱的工人。

examples.en: The party was casual, so nobody dressed up.
examples.cn: 聚会很随意，所以没人特意打扮。

examples.en: He made a casual remark about the weather.
examples.cn: 他随口说了句天气的话。

examples.en: The factory takes on casual workers at harvest time.
examples.cn: 工厂在收获季节雇临时工。

dict_mnemonic.text: casual 里有 case：把生活看成一件件偶然落下的 case，穿着随意、说话随口都叫 casual。

root: 源自拉丁语 casualis（偶然的），再由 casus（落下、事件）派生，与 case 同根。

sensesIntro.en: What happens by chance needs no ceremony, no care and no long contract, so one root yields informality, carelessness and temporary work.
sensesIntro.cn: 偶然发生的事既不需要仪式，也不需要用心和长期合同，于是一个词根给出随意、马虎和临时这三层意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something that simply falls out without plan.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有计划、自己落下来的事。

branches.en: Chance work is work without a long agreement.
branches.cn: 偶然来的工作就是没有长期约定的工作。

branches.en: An occasion without ceremony lets clothes become casual.
branches.cn: 不带仪式的场合格调，让穿着也变得休闲。

branches.en: A remark made without thought is the careless side of the same root.
branches.cn: 未经思考的话就是同一词根的马虎一面。

branches.en: Both senses lack preparation, one in style and one in attention.
branches.cn: 两个义项都缺准备，一个缺在风格，一个缺在注意力。

branches.en: Relaxed dress and short-term work both sit outside formal rules.
branches.cn: 休闲着装与短期工作都处在正式规则之外。

intro.en: Casual takes the -ly and -ness endings and one old noun, casualty, that drifted far from its root.
intro.cn: casual 接 -ly 与 -ness 词尾，另有一个离开词根很远的旧名词 casualty。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin casualis, from casus, the same event word behind case and occasion.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 casualis，出自 casus，与 case、occasion 共享同一个事件词。

items.example: The casualness of the office surprised him.
items.exampleCN: 办公室的随意气氛让他吃惊。

items.meaning: a day when informal dress is allowed
items.meaningCN: 允许穿休闲装的工作日
items.exampleCN: 休闲星期五是上个月开始的。

items.example: Casualis is the Latin source of casual.
items.exampleCN: casualis 是 casual 的拉丁语来源。
casus 也是英语 case 的来源。

latinEntries.exampleCN: casualis 形容没有计划的事件。

latinEntries.example: Casus lies behind case and casual.
latinEntries.exampleCN: casus 是 case 与 casual 的源头。
